precepts.label: Habakkuk 3:14
precepts.why:
Officer Tatum was asked if black men like him were better off during slavery, and he answered, 100 percent. He said that after slavery there was an explosion of success, black Wall Street, men married to the women they had children with, and now look at the inner cities. What he does not understand is that he thinks white people just switched and started loving us after they let us out of slavery.

“Thou didst strike through with his staves the head of his villages: they came out as a whirlwind to scatter me”. When Christ returns, these same people who had us in slavery, and have us in slavery, are going to try to fight against Christ.

“their rejoicing was as to devour the poor secretly.” These same slave owners rejoice to devour the poor, and they do it secretly. Even though slavery supposedly ended with the emancipation proclamation in 1863, then what? You had the school to prison pipeline. Redlining. Sundown towns. Sharecropping. It is still the same thing.

Look at us now, and why? Because he is setting up all these traps. That is why he is still oppressing us to this day, and that is the “yoke of iron upon thy neck, until he have destroyed thee.” But Tatum cannot see that.

precepts.label: Isaiah 14:32
precepts.why:
Habakkuk said their rejoicing is “to devour the poor secretly.” Who are the poor? “What shall one then answer the messengers of the nation? That the Lord hath founded Zion, and the poor of his people shall trust in it.”

The poor of his people. We are the poor that they are devouring secretly. The poor are Israel, and it is Zion that the Lord founded for them to trust in.

Tatum blames the murders, the violent crime and the abortions in the inner cities on our people alone. But who legalized abortion? The white people. Who started Planned Parenthood with Margaret Sanger? He just skips past that; according to him they are not the cause. That is the secret devouring of the poor, and it is the yoke of iron of Deuteronomy 28:48 still on our neck.

precepts.label: Acts 24:16
precepts.why:
Tatum said black people need to do better: y’all whole life is activism, y’all still complaining and protesting like y’all still slaves. Why were the brothers in Ocean Springs, Mississippi? Because one of our brothers, Nolan Wells, had a mysterious death with a bunch of white people around it, in a town known for lynching black people. Yes, we are activists. Yes, we stand up for righteousness and speak against the evils and atrocities that happen to our people. That puts fear in our oppressors, and he is doing their bidding: hey, you’ve been cooning great lately.

So what is better than standing up for God and standing up for his people? “And herein do I exercise myself, to have always a conscience void of offence toward God, and toward men.”

We always have to do what is right toward God and toward our people. Better looks like getting your household in order, not committing fornication and adultery, taking care of your family. What is better than that? That is what a conscience void of offence looks like, and he is not speaking from the point of a black man.

precepts.label: Nehemiah 9:27
precepts.why:
“Therefore thou deliveredst them into the hand of their enemies, who vexed them”. That is what happened to us: we have been delivered into the hands of our enemies, the yoke of iron of Deuteronomy 28:48.

“and in the time of their trouble, when they cried unto thee, thou heardest them from heaven”. That is what is happening now. The Lord is starting to hear our cry. We are supposed to pray unto the Lord until he brings vengeance; that is what the Bible tells us to do.

“and according to thy manifold mercies thou gavest them saviours, who saved them out of the hand of their enemies.” How is that happening? By the purple and gold going to this city and that city, this country and that country, teaching the word of God. These are the saviours, and the saviours showed up in Ocean Springs, Mississippi.

So when we see these things happen to our people, yes, we are going to be there, and no, we are not going to stop. We don’t care if we have coons among our own people; we are going to rise up and save the day, because that is how God ordained it. Tatum is mad about it. Get mad. You hate your people and you hate your God.

precepts.label: Exodus 7:4
precepts.why:
A 1966 CBS documentary, Black Power, White Backlash, went into Cicero, Illinois, where 15,000 black people worked in the factories every day but not a single black family lived, and every one of them had to leave when the sun went down. A resident said there are many good coloreds, but the ones that are going to march, I don’t like.

They do not like it when we march, because when we march we have our pride, our dignity, our respect and our confidence. They do not like when we stand up as the nation of Israel; it angers them and it makes them afraid. We have been marching; Marcus Garvey was marching back in the day.

“But Pharaoh shall not hearken unto you, that I may lay my hand upon Egypt, and bring forth mine armies, and my people the children of Israel, out of the land of Egypt by great judgments.” Mine armies. We have been marching since Egypt, and we marched around the walls of Jericho.

Israel came out of Egypt as the armies of the Lord, by great judgments on the ones who held them. That is why our marching troubles our oppressors.

precepts.label: Revelation 11:11
precepts.why:
They do not like when we stand up on our feet with confidence as the nation of Israel, not as blacks, but as the nation of Israel.

“And after three days and an half the Spirit of life from God entered into them, and they stood upon their feet; and great fear fell upon them which saw them.”

Great fear falls on them when they see us rise up as the children of God, as the army of the living God. That is what the man in Cicero feared when he said he could not stand the ones who march, and it is what puts fear in our oppressors when the brothers show up in a town like Ocean Springs. The yoke of iron destroyed us, but the Spirit of life from God stands us back on our feet.

precepts.label: 2 Chronicles 17:9
precepts.why:
Tatum claimed he had not seen black Hebrew Israelites going out and saying anything in the community when a black man died. That is a lie; he has been found a liar. That is what we do literally every week. We teach in the hoods and the ghettos where our people are: O Block in Chicago, East St. Louis, Memphis, Miami, Compton, LA, Philly. We go toe to toe and face our people.

“And they taught in Judah, and had the book of the law of the Lord with them, and went about throughout all the cities of Judah, and taught the people.”

They taught in Judah: we go to our people just like the forefathers did. They had the book of the law of the Lord with them: we bring the Bible with us. They went throughout all the cities: we do not just go to one city or one state. Wherever our people are scattered, wherever our people are being afflicted, we are there, teaching the people.

precepts.label: Matthew 15:24
precepts.why:
A pastor named Pam declared that the gospel cannot be for one ethnicity only, that it cannot be just for black men or for white men, and that this is a heretical doctrine preached by false, cultic ministries. Either the cultic ministries are right or Jesus is right; somebody is wrong. It’s you, Pam.

“But he answered and said, I am not sent but unto the lost sheep of the house of Israel.”

It is only for one nation, twelve tribes. If you are not part of that, you are not getting in. Some of our people are bugged the hell out, and it is a direct correlation to slavery. A white pastor even said God blessed black Americans through white people and slavery, and Tatum agrees with that. But Christ was sent to the lost sheep of the house of Israel, the same people under the yoke of iron of Deuteronomy 28:48.

precepts.label: Revelation 21:12
precepts.why:
The holy city “had a wall great and high, and had twelve gates, and at the gates twelve angels, and names written thereon, which are the names of the twelve tribes of the children of Israel”.

Praises to the Most High for that. The kingdom is only for God’s people. The gates of the city carry the names of the twelve tribes, and no other nation’s name is written there.

That settles what Pam called heresy. Christ was not sent but unto the lost sheep of the house of Israel, and the city he brings has twelve gates for the twelve tribes. The same people the Lord sent into bondage with a yoke of iron upon their neck are the people whose names are on the gates.

precepts.label: Deuteronomy 33:25
precepts.why:
Moses blessed the tribes “before his death”, and of Asher he said “Let Asher be blessed with children; let him be acceptable to his brethren, and let him dip his foot in oil.” Asher is Venezuela, Colombia, Peru, Brazil, from Colombia down to Uruguay. When the conquistadors came to conquer, rob and pillage, many fled into the jungles of the Amazon and grew up without fathers, so they must be made acceptable to their brethren, and we have to go there and save our people in the jungles. And the oil: a brother in Venezuela, asked how Venezuelans and Colombians can benefit from their precious resource, stood right on the oil. The oil is the precious commodity the red man covets so earnestly.

Then verse 25: “Thy shoes shall be iron and brass.” Look up the name Brazil: it is associated with the Hebrew word barzel, meaning iron. It is not a coincidence that the name Brazil means iron in Hebrew; these people know where our people are. Brazil is full of iron, Colombia is full of iron, Venezuela is full of iron, Ecuador is full of iron. Mexico has iron too, but not the same abundance as South America.

“and as thy days, so shall thy strength be.” That is the inheritance of our people in these lands. It is not a coincidence, the names these countries get, for those who do not believe that the northern kingdom is the northern kingdom.

The elders in the 60s and 70s deciphered this without Google or the internet; all they had were the scriptures and history books. Now, in the information age, it is so much plainer. Asher's blessing, children, oil, iron and brass, sits right where the Bible said it would.

precepts.label: Revelation 11:15
precepts.why:
At Jericho it was sevens all the way through: “seven priests shall bear before the ark seven trumpets of rams’ horns: and the seventh day ye shall compass the city seven times, and the priests shall blow with the trumpets.” Six days they went round once, and on the seventh day, the Sabbath day, seven times. “And it came to pass at the seventh time, when the priests blew with the trumpets, Joshua said unto the people, Shout; for the Lord hath given you the city.” Because of their faith, on the seventh day the Most High brought the walls down flat.

Revelation shows the same pattern at the end: “And the seventh angel sounded; and there were great voices in heaven, saying, The kingdoms of this world are become the kingdoms of our Lord, and of his Christ; and he shall reign for ever and ever.” The seventh angel sounded the trump, and that brought forth completion. It is the same thing that happened when our forefathers walked around the walls of Jericho.

Seven represents completion and totality, and it also represents complete deliverance. Nothing is accidental with the Most High; he uses seven as a form of deliverance. From the beginning it has been there: the seventh day rest, Naaman dipped seven times, and Jericho compassed seven times by seven priests with seven trumpets.

So the seventh trumpet at Jericho gave Israel the city, and the seventh trumpet in Revelation gives the kingdoms of this world to our Lord and his Christ. All of this is a representation of Christ, and it points to the complete deliverance of Israel when he reigns.

classes.title: The Nativity: the Bloodline, Birthright, & the Messiah

precepts.label: Judges 21:25
precepts.why:
Naomi told Ruth, “Behold, thy sister in law is gone back unto her people, and unto her gods”. Orpah went back to Moab, to her people and her gods. These were not Israelite women; this was a heathen woman of another nation. That is important, because there are doctrines out there teaching that Ruth was an Israelite. No, she was not. She was a heathen. Was it right for Boaz to deal with a heathen? No, but it happened.

Just in case there is any confusion, the last verse of Judges, right above Ruth, shows why it happened: “In those days there was no king in Israel: every man did that which was right in his own eyes.” During the judges, we did what we wanted to do.

And Ruth opens in that very time: “Now it came to pass in the days when the judges ruled”. There was no king. It was the time when Israel did what they wanted, and that included taking heathen women.

So Ruth's story does not make her an Israelite, and it does not make it right to take a heathen wife. It shows what Israel was doing when every man did what was right in his own eyes. The scripture keeps calling her what she is: “Ruth the Moabitess”. That is clear.

precepts.label: Zechariah 8:23
precepts.why:
Ruth said, “thy people shall be my people, and thy God my God”. She is a heathen saying, if I go with you, I will be as if I am an Israelite, and I will serve your God too. She is cleaving to an Israelite woman, that's all; there were no promises made to her. “Where thou diest, will I die, and there will I be buried”: I'm not leaving you.

The nations are going to be the same way in the kingdom. Zechariah shows it: “Thus saith the Lord of hosts; In those days it shall come to pass, that ten men shall take hold out of all languages of the nations, even shall take hold of the skirt of him that is a Jew, saying, We will go with you: for we have heard that God is with you.”

We will go with you, just like Ruth said. For we have heard that God is with you: your God is a real God, and ours is garbage. They are going to cleave to Israel the way Ruth cleaved to Naomi, and they will cleave as servants.

So Ruth is the picture of the nations in the kingdom: not Israelites, but holding on to Israel because the God of Israel is the true God.

thread.label: Ruth 4:5-10
thread.text: Then said Boaz, What day thou buyest the field of the hand of Naomi, thou must buy it also of Ruth the Moabitess, the wife of the dead, to raise up the name of the dead upon his inheritance.

classes.title: The Nativity: the Bloodline, Birthright, & the Messiah

precepts.label: John 4:3-5
precepts.why:
Ruth 4 is a trial at the gate before ten elders over land. Elimelech had land; he died, and his two sons, Mahlon and Chilion, died too, leaving no man to take it. So the land had to be taken up by the next of kin. Boaz told the nearer kinsman that Naomi “selleth a parcel of land, which was our brother Elimelech’s.” A parcel of land: that phrase opens the whole chapter.

John 4 uses the same wording. Christ “must needs go through Samaria. Then cometh he to a city of Samaria, which is called Sychar, near to the parcel of ground that Jacob gave to his son Joseph.” Jacob gave Joseph that parcel of ground; he bought his son that land.

A parcel of land, a parcel of ground, a parcel of a field: they are all the same thing, and a parcel of land and an inheritance are one and the same. So when Boaz bought the parcel that was Elimelech's, he was not making an ordinary purchase. He was taking up an inheritance in Israel, one that had to stay in the family of the dead.

precepts.label: Genesis 33:18-20
precepts.why:
Genesis 33 gives the history behind the “parcel of ground that Jacob gave to his son Joseph” in John 4. “Jacob came to Shalem, a city of Shechem, which is in the land of Canaan, when he came from Padan–aram; and pitched his tent before the city. And he bought a parcel of a field, where he had spread his tent, at the hand of the children of Hamor, Shechem’s father, for an hundred pieces of money.”

Jacob bought that land from the Hamites for a hundred pieces of money, and “he erected there an altar, and called it El–elohe–Israel.” A parcel of a field is again the same thing as a parcel of land: an inheritance.

Later, as he was dying, Israel told Joseph, “Moreover I have given to thee one portion above thy brethren, which I took out of the hand of the Amorite with my sword and with my bow.” His sons did take the land by the sword; Simeon and Levi went crazy and killed the men of that city. But the field was bought first, before his sons ever took it. So the inheritance at Shechem stood on a lawful purchase, the same way Boaz bought Elimelech's parcel before the elders at the gate.

precepts.label: Joshua 24:32
precepts.why:
“And the bones of Joseph, which the children of Israel brought up out of Egypt, buried they in Shechem, in a parcel of ground which Jacob bought of the sons of Hamor the father of Shechem for an hundred pieces of silver: and it became the inheritance of the children of Joseph.” The parcel of ground, the parcel of land, the parcel of a field is the land of inheritance, and this one was given to Ephraim.

That is what Boaz was protecting in Ruth 4. The nearer kinsman would not redeem it, “lest I mar mine own inheritance”, and plucked off his shoe; here the shoe is passed without shame, because he is yielding the right to someone else, not refusing his brother. Boaz bought all that was Elimelech's, Chilion's and Mahlon's, and took Ruth, the wife of Mahlon, “to raise up the name of the dead upon his inheritance, that the name of the dead be not cut off from among his brethren.” The son he raised up would inherit that land, because it belonged to Mahlon. Boaz is still the father; Boaz begat Obed, and the line goes through Boaz. There are no two fathers. The land falls under the dead man's line; the lineage goes back to Boaz. That is love your neighbor as yourself.

So Elimelech did not lose his land. We kept our land in house. Land is very important: if you have it, keep it and give it to your children; don't sell it off. Our people once had millions of acres in America, and Esau made laws, eminent domain among them, and found a distant kin to pay off with a little money, and so stole millions of acres, beaches included, from Judah.

The allotment still stands. When we came out of Egypt, every family was allotted land, and Judges says “the children of Israel went every man unto his inheritance to possess the land.” Those families are here today. The Lord says he “will bring them again, every man to his heritage, and every man to his land.” Whoever is left after the destruction, those who repent, will be given back the land and inheritance that was given to us back then.

precepts.label: Jeremiah 12:15
precepts.why:
“And Salmon begat Boaz, and Boaz begat Obed”. Boaz raised up seed in the name of Mahlon, but the record says Boaz begat Obed, not Mahlon, because Mahlon was dead. The genealogy goes under Boaz; the land falls under the dead man's line. Obed takes on the land of Elimelech even though that is not his father's line. That is the inheritance: the parcel of land, the parcel of field, the parcel of ground. You don't inherit a tribe; you inherit the land. And they were both of the same tribe anyway.

That is why the scripture says this in Jeremiah: “And it shall come to pass, after that I have plucked them out I will return, and have compassion on them, and will bring them again, every man to his heritage, and every man to his land.” It literally means what it says. In the beginning God allotted every family land.

The line of David had an inheritance given to it; the families of Judah each had land appointed to them. Guess what? Those families are here today. When the Lord returns, those that make it, that repented, are going back to that land, every man to his heritage.

That is why Boaz raised up seed for Elimelech's family: so the land would stay within that family's inheritance. That is loving your neighbor as yourself. We kept our land in house. So land is very important: if you have it, keep it and give it to your kids; don't just sell it off. A lot of Judah had millions of acres here in America, and Esau stole them, creating laws like eminent domain and finding some distant kin to pay a little money and take the land. There are beaches that belong to us. But the Lord will bring every man again to his heritage and to his land.

precepts.label: Judges 2:6
precepts.why:
Judges shows how the land was first given: “And when Joshua had let the people go, the children of Israel went every man unto his inheritance to possess the land.” We all had land and an inheritance. When we came out of Egypt, every family was allotted land. Whoever of those same families is left after the destruction takes place will be given back the land and inheritance that was given to us back then.

Notice it says every man unto his inheritance. Sisters, you're divorcing us and taking half our stuff, but it says every man. Our wives benefit from our inheritance; it belongs to the men, but it is theirs too because they are married to us. According to God, the inheritance belongs to the men, just as the earth belonged to Adam, and Eve benefitted from it because she was helping him.

And the land we inherit is not an acre or something. 1 Chronicles 2 shows Jair “who had three and twenty cities in the land of Gilead”, “even threescore cities”. We owned cities. Somebody literally owned the Bronx, Manhattan, Brooklyn, Queens. We had castles on those cities, winter houses and summer houses.

That is why the land in Ruth had to stay with Elimelech's family. Boaz begat Obed, and the genealogy goes through Boaz down to Jesse and David, but the inheritance, every man's portion from the time of Joshua, stayed with the dead man's line through the seed raised up to him.

thread.text: And Elisha sent a messenger unto him, saying, Go and wash in Jordan seven times, and thy flesh shall come again to thee, and thou shalt be clean.

classes.title: 70 Times 7: The Perfection of Mercy Through Christ

precepts.label: Isaiah 1:16-20
precepts.why:
Naaman was told, “Wash, and be clean”, and when he believed and obeyed the word of the prophet, he was clean. Isaiah shows what the true washing is: “Wash you, make you clean; put away the evil of your doings from before mine eyes; cease to do evil; Learn to do well”.

Put away the evil of your doings: that's the true washing. Cease to do evil, learn to do well. Action, action, action. Not speak well, do well. “seek judgment, relieve the oppressed, judge the fatherless, plead for the widow.”

“though your sins be as scarlet”, bloodshot red, “they shall be as white as snow”, if you learn to do well. “though they be red like crimson, they shall be as wool.” But it hangs on obedience: “If ye be willing and obedient, ye shall eat the good of the land: But if ye refuse and rebel, ye shall be devoured with the sword”.

That is Naaman. At first he refused and went away in a rage. When he humbled himself and did according to the saying of the man of God, his flesh came again like the flesh of a little child. His belief and his obedience are what made him clean.

precepts.label: Psalms 51:6-7
precepts.why:
Naaman believed that the word of the prophet would heal him if he followed the commandment, going down to the river Jordan and dipping seven times. That belief is what healed him of his leprosy.

David prays the same way: “Behold, thou desirest truth in the inward parts: and in the hidden part thou shalt make me to know wisdom.” Truth in the inward parts is what the Most High desires. Then: “Purge me with hyssop, and I shall be clean: wash me, and I shall be whiter than snow.”

The water of the Jordan did not do it by itself; the Jordan was muddy water, and Naaman would rather have had the rivers of Damascus. The word of God is what really cleanses us of our sins. Naaman obeyed the word, and he was made clean, his flesh like the flesh of a little child.

precepts.label: Luke 3:3-4
precepts.why:
We read about Naaman going down into the river Jordan to be cleansed. Luke brings us back to that same river: John “came into all the country about Jordan, preaching the baptism of repentance for the remission of sins; As it is written in the book of the words of Esaias the prophet, saying, The voice of one crying in the wilderness, Prepare ye the way of the Lord, make his paths straight.”

The baptism of repentance, for the remission of sins, preached about Jordan. Naaman was washed of his leprosy in the Jordan, and John preached the washing away of sins in the same Jordan. Nothing is accidental with the Most High.

It was Christ who healed Naaman, working through Elisha by his spirit. And John in the Jordan was preparing the way of that same Lord.

precepts.label: Matthew 3:13
precepts.why:
“Then cometh Jesus from Galilee to Jordan unto John, to be baptized of him.” Christ went unto John the Baptist to be baptized, and in what river? Jordan: the same river that Naaman had to dip in seven times.

Seven represents completion. Naaman dipped seven times in Jordan, completion in the river Jordan, and his flesh came again like the flesh of a little child. The number and the river both point to the same Christ.

Who did the healing for Naaman? Not Elisha on his own. Elisha was working by the spirit of Christ; Christ is the one who did the healing, and he used Elisha as the prophet. So when Christ himself comes to the Jordan, it is the same one who cleansed Naaman there, the one who makes us clean.

precepts.label: Luke 4:25-27
precepts.why:
Christ himself reached back and referenced this exact history. “I tell you of a truth, many widows were in Israel in the days of Elias, when the heaven was shut up three years and six months, when great famine was throughout all the land; But unto none of them was Elias sent, save unto Sarepta, a city of Sidon, unto a woman that was a widow.”

Then the point: “And many lepers were in Israel in the time of Eliseus the prophet; and none of them was cleansed, saving Naaman the Syrian.” Of all the lepers, the one cleansed was the one who humbled himself, believed, and went down and dipped seven times according to the saying of the man of God.

And seven also represents complete deliverance. Naaman dipped seven times and was delivered from his leprosy; Christ, the one whose spirit healed him through Elisha, spoke of it himself.

precepts.label: 2 Kings 25:27-28
precepts.why:
Zedekiah rebelled like his brother and his nephew did. He tried to run away and got caught in the plains of Jericho, and they killed his kids in front of him first, then took his eyes out, bound him and locked him up in Babylon. At this point there are no more kings of Judah; Zedekiah was the last one. His sons are gone, his heirs are gone. So who's left?

Read on: “in the seven and thirtieth year of the captivity of Jehoiachin king of Judah”, “Evil–merodach king of Babylon in the year that he began to reign did lift up the head of Jehoiachin king of Judah out of prison; And he spake kindly to him, and set his throne above the throne of the kings that were with him in Babylon”. Jehoiachin had been locked up between 36 and 37 years. Then he “changed his prison garments: and he did eat bread continually before him all the days of his life.” His allowance was a continual allowance, a daily rate for every day: Babylon gave him a job and status.

Jehoiachin is Jeconiah, and he is the Jechonias of Matthew 1:11. He got some mercy in captivity, but was he a king anymore at this point? No. He was a king, but now he was a captive in Babylon, receiving wages and some status.

And in Babylon he had children: “the sons of Jeconiah; Assir, Salathiel his son”. Salathiel is Shealtiel, the father of Zerubbabel, whose name means born in Babylon. That is where the line of the kings of Judah went on after Zedekiah's sons were slain: through a captive king in Babylon.

thread.text: The sons also of Hezron, that were born unto him; Jerahmeel, and Ram, and Chelubai.

precepts.label: 1 Kings 4:31
precepts.why:
Judah had five sons: Er, Onan and Shelah by the daughter of Shua the Canaanitess, and the twins Pharez and Zerah by Tamar. “The sons of Pharez; Hezron, and Hamul. And the sons of Zerah; Zimri, and Ethan, and Heman, and Calcol, and Dara: five of them in all.” Ethan, Heman, Calcol and Dara became very famous. They were very wise.

How wise? Solomon’s wisdom is measured against them: “For he was wiser than all men; than Ethan the Ezrahite, and Heman, and Chalcol, and Darda, the sons of Mahol: and his fame was in all nations round about.”

Those same sons of Judah were so wise that many men were named after them, and Solomon surpassed even them. He was wiser than the wise men of his own tribe.

That is the house this genealogy runs through. Hezron, the oldest son of Pharez, begat Ram, and from Ram comes Amminadab, Nahshon, Salma, Boaz, Obed and Jesse: a tribe of wise men, princes and kings.

precepts.label: Numbers 2:3
precepts.why:
“And Ram begat Amminadab; and Amminadab begat Nahshon, prince of the children of Judah”. Nahshon was of the elite princes of Judah, a prince family, a royal family. The census confirms the same man: “Of Judah; Nahshon the son of Amminadab.”

And in the camp: “And on the east side toward the rising of the sun shall they of the standard of the camp of Judah pitch throughout their armies: and Nahshon the son of Amminadab shall be captain of the children of Judah.”

So Nahshon was a captain. These men had serious status: princes and captains, leaders. They were warriors; they were not regular men.

“And Nahshon begat Salma, and Salma begat Boaz, And Boaz begat Obed, and Obed begat Jesse”. Boaz came from that line, the line of Pharez, the twin that breached, not the one whose hand came out first with the scarlet thread. And Jesse had eight sons, and one of those sons is David.

precepts.label: Exodus 6:23
precepts.why:
Now a tie-in regarding family ties: “And Aaron took him Elisheba, daughter of Amminadab, sister of Naashon, to wife; and she bare him Nadab, and Abihu, Eleazar, and Ithamar.”

Aaron is Moses’ brother, of Levi. He took Elisheba, Amminadab’s daughter and Nahshon’s sister, to wife. Aaron’s wife was of the tribe of Judah. Those families intermarried, priests and kings marrying together. It is no coincidence; that is why John the Baptist and Christ are cousins.

Nadab and Abihu were the two who offered strange fire and were killed; Eleazar and Ithamar were spared. Eleazar became the high priest in the days of Joshua, the mediator before the Lord. So Eleazar’s mama was Judah. That is why some Levites don’t have the big heads; their mama is Judah. And don’t forget the big nose, too.

So Amminadab begat Nahshon and a daughter Elisheba. Aaron married Elisheba and had the four sons, the high priests, which makes Nahshon Aaron’s brother-in-law. And from Nahshon came Salma, Boaz, Obed and Jesse: the priesthood and the royal line of Judah bound together in one family.

precepts.label: Genesis 15:3-4
precepts.why:
Abram, childless, was going to leave his house to Eliezer of Damascus, the eldest servant born in his house: “Behold, to me thou hast given no seed: and, lo, one born in my house is mine heir.” The Lord said no: “This shall not be thine heir; but he that shall come forth out of thine own bowels shall be thine heir.” Not a heathen servant, but his own seed. An heir and an inheritance are the same word, like a family heirloom passed down the line.

That is the key to 1 Chronicles 2: “Now Sheshan had no sons, but daughters. And Sheshan had a servant, an Egyptian, whose name was Jarha. And Sheshan gave his daughter to Jarha his servant to wife.” This was while Israel was in Egypt, when we had no land of inheritance allotted to us. People read it and say the Egyptian married into the tribe and became Judah. No.

The record follows that line for generation after generation so that it is known. When Israel came out of Egypt and inherited the land, that line could not receive land, because the land passes by the paternal bloodline and that line goes back to an Egyptian servant. They were among us in the land, but they did not inherit. It is written there to exclude, not to include. Sheshan's brothers had sons and received land; his line did not. It does not mean the Egyptian became a Jew. When we came back under the Persians and the Medes, a man who could not show from his father's house who he came from was given no inheritance, and a Levite could not serve in his office. Zerubbabel could show he came from King David's line.

The daughters of Zelophehad show the law when a man has only daughters. They asked, “Why should the name of our father be done away from among his family, because he hath no son?” The Lord said, “If a man die, and have no son, then ye shall cause his inheritance to pass unto his daughter”, then to his brother, then his father's brethren, then the next kinsman: the law Boaz was fulfilling. But those daughters had to marry “only to the family of the tribe of their father”, “So shall not the inheritance of the children of Israel remove from tribe to tribe.” The inheritance of Israel is paternal. There is no sin in marrying a woman of another tribe; Aaron did it. The command there was only to keep the land in the tribe. We have no land in captivity now, so marry within your nation and stay with your people.

precepts.label: 1 Chronicles 28:19
precepts.why:
David, chosen out of Judah and out of his father’s house, hands the building of the house to the son the Lord chose to sit on the throne: “Solomon thy son, he shall build my house and my courts: for I have chosen him to be my son, and I will be his father.” “Moreover I will establish his kingdom for ever”. Solomon’s kingdom, not Solomon and his brethren’s. Then David charges him: “Take heed now; for the Lord hath chosen thee to build an house for the sanctuary: be strong, and do it.”

“Then David gave to Solomon his son the pattern of the porch”. The blueprints to the temple: guess who gave them to Solomon? David. Solomon did not come up with the design; David came up with it, and Solomon fulfilled his father’s wishes. That porch is why the feast of dedication is kept at Solomon’s porch. It took Solomon seven years to build the temple and thirteen years to build his own house, so the temple was done before his house was finished.

David gave him the pattern “of the houses thereof, and of the treasuries thereof, and of the upper chambers thereof”, the floors and levels, “and of the inner parlours thereof, and of the place of the mercy seat”, the holy of holies. “And the pattern of all that he had by the spirit”: the spirit moved David to design the temple. The courses of the priests, which priest for burning incense and which for each service, David was behind all of that too. Gold by weight for the things of gold, “refined gold by weight” for the altar of incense, everything gold, “and gold for the pattern of the chariot of the cherubims, that spread out their wings, and covered the ark of the covenant of the Lord.”

“All this, said David, the Lord made me understand in writing by his hand upon me, even all the works of this pattern.” David did not write it off the top of his head. The Lord moved his hand on what to write, and David drew out the temple through his hands. So the house Solomon built on the throne of the kingdom of the Lord was the Lord’s own pattern, given through David to the son chosen to sit on David’s throne.

Maccabees shows the Greeks doing it: they “laid open the book of the law, wherein the heathen had sought to paint the likeness of their images.” They opened our Bibles, and the heathen, the Greeks, sought to paint the likeness of their images in our Bibles. The Father has divine essence, the Holy Spirit has divine essence, the Son has divine essence, so when Christ came on the earth keeping humanity and godhood, he is his own god. So if Christ is the essence of his Father, then Christ becomes the God of his own humanity, God over his own flesh. It's madness. precepts.label: Deuteronomy 28:47
precepts.why:
“Because thou servedst not the Lord thy God with joyfulness, and with gladness of heart, for the abundance of all things”. So-called Christmas, Thanksgiving and so-called New Year's are pagan, evil hella days, not holy days. How can you talk about Thanksgiving on stolen land?

“For the customs of the people are vain”, void of anything credible: “one cutteth a tree out of the forest”, and “They deck it with silver and with gold”. That was the custom in the Babylonian empire, four empires before Christ was born in the time of Rome. What do lights, tin and silver on a tree have to do with Christ? Nothing. It is Sol Invictus, the unconquered sun, sun worship commemorating Nimrod, Tammuz, whom the women wept for in Ezekiel 8, celebrated on December 25th. Our people know Christ has nothing to do with it, the same way the Bible gives no white Jesus, but they will not stand up for truth.

Serving the gods of the nations instead of serving the Lord with gladness is what put us under our enemies. Anybody who continues to celebrate that madness now knows better and will be judged by the Most High.

precepts.label: Deuteronomy 32:30
precepts.why:
“Behold, how good and how pleasant it is for brethren to dwell together in unity!” Why is that good and pleasant? It's the only way we grow, keeping the commandments together as a unit; without unity there is disorder, and nothing gets built. But the reason it is so important is that we can't be stopped when we are unified. Moses shows it: “How should one chase a thousand, and two put ten thousand to flight”?

Unity. That's how we are going to do it: through us together, unified in Christ. Hence the name Israel United in Christ. We can move mountains. It's that type of unity we have to come to and understand, because without it, brothers, we won't do nothing.

Look at some of the others, not doing anything. They don't aspire to do anything; they're fine just where they're at, cool just being in the house, and they will keep doing videos from their garages. But we have worldwide goals. The vision here has been set at a worldwide standard. If you don't have worldwide aspirations, you're not going to do worldwide things. If you think small, you'll stay small. Shoot for the stars.

The sixty-man camp of 2013 showed it: that small number organized and unified set a standard in the nation, and today one phone call could bring a thousand men. That is one chasing a thousand and two putting ten thousand to flight, when brethren dwell together in unity.

precepts.label: Ecclesiasticus 25:1
precepts.why:
“Behold, how good and how pleasant it is for brethren to dwell together in unity!” Some think this is just talking about a bunch of Negroes coming together, a bunch of brothers together, and that's beautiful. No, it is much more than that. If you are spiritual, you understand this unity is not gang banging, not the Hoovers, not the Omegas, Kappas and Alphas, not Freemasonry, none of that worldly nonsense some of us came out of. It is being unified in Christ; hence the name Israel United in Christ.

Sirach shows what unity God is beautified by: “In three things I was beautified, and stood up beautiful both before God and men: the unity of brethren, the love of neighbours, a man and a wife that agree together.”

The unity of brethren in what? In righteousness. The love of neighbours is not that oogly googly feeling, that's my neighbor, we're good friends; it is unity in righteousness, someone that shows care for their nation and their people. A man and a wife that agree together, in righteousness: a sanctified holy marriage that has come together in the Lord is a beautiful thing before the Lord.

Anything other than that is not beautiful, and the Lord is not beautified by it. Remember how Paul wrote to the different schools: you are puffed up, there are all types of schisms among you. That is not unity. To be unified means to come together in holiness and righteousness, the way God meant it to be and the way Christ told us to be. And that unification of the nation of Israel is the highest known threat to this evil world; it scares them.

You are not Israel anymore, you are not keeping the commandments, you do not have faith in Christ; you have faith in white Jesus and in the white man. God made you into a Christian dummy.

When you are a Christian you do not know it, so you say strange things and strange doctrines, like the burning mountain is a meteorite. Look at the black pastor today, preaching a sermon while getting a haircut: soft, sweet, moist, squishy, and a leader in the black church. That is the result when the law departs out of the mouth of those who are supposed to teach it.

So Psalms 137:6 is the curse on the tongue for forgetting Jerusalem, and Joshua 1:8 is what the tongue was made for: the law, spoken and meditated on day and night, so that we may observe to do all that is written therein.

“Blessed be the Lord my strength, which teacheth my hands to war, and my fingers to fight.” We serve a God of war, the God that formed the light and created darkness, and that God of war is Christ. David is speaking of how the Lord equipped him with his mighty fighting skills, and the same man of war teaches his soldiers to do the same. Paul says it: “Thou therefore endure hardness, as a good soldier of Jesus Christ. No man that warreth entangleth himself with the affairs of this life; that he may please him who hath chosen him to be a soldier.”

The God of war handpicked every one of us to be soldiers in his mighty army. We are in a boot camp, a training camp, and he is teaching us how to war. Some brothers think they are here just for the unleavened bread, just to be around the brothers. No. Everything going on in the earth, in your household and in the congregation is a teachable moment, because there are spirits in all of it, and we are being built up to deal with those spirits.

It is a process. You start with yourself, subduing your own body, and that is ongoing until you go in the grave. Then your household, then the congregation, as a leader helping other brothers and sisters do the same. Even when you hear somebody else being corrected, it is about you, because at some point you will stand in that same position.

Judges shows why the nations are here: “Now these are the nations which the Lord left, to prove Israel by them”, “to teach them war.” The nations are the Lord's sword to teach us war. If you think that means go get your Glock, you are being simple. “For though we walk in the flesh, we do not war after the flesh.” At Ai the Lord said, “I have given into thy hand the king of Ai”, and still told Joshua, “lay thee an ambush for the city behind it.” The victory is already ordained, but you must go about it the way the Lord commanded. The spiritual side of the war is obedience.

So endure hardness. Some send emails saying, I am no longer with IUIC, I am going to take a break. Taking a break from the Lord? That will not work. A good soldier does not entangle himself with the affairs of this life; he stays in the fight to please the one who chose him.

thread.label: Proverbs 9:1
thread.text: Wisdom hath builded her house, she hath hewn out her seven pillars:

classes.title: 70 Times 7: The Perfection of Mercy Through Christ

precepts.label: Proverbs 8:22-23
precepts.why:
“Wisdom hath builded her house”. Who is this wisdom? Go back a chapter, where wisdom speaks: “The Lord possessed me in the beginning of his way, before his works of old. I was set up from everlasting, from the beginning, or ever the earth was.”

This is going into Christ and wisdom, one and the same, interchangeable. Christ is the ultimate wisdom, the complete wisdom, set up from everlasting before the earth was.

That is why chapter 9 says wisdom “hath hewn out her seven pillars”. Seven represents completion, and Christ is complete wisdom. The house wisdom built stands on him, the one the Lord possessed in the beginning of his way.

precepts.label: Isaiah 11:1-2
precepts.why:
Wisdom “hath hewn out her seven pillars”. Let's see who this wisdom pertains to and who had these seven pillars. Isaiah: “And there shall come forth a rod out of the stem of Jesse, and a Branch shall grow out of his roots”. That is talking about Christ.

Now count what rests upon him. “And the spirit of the Lord shall rest upon him”: that's one. “the spirit of wisdom”: two. “and understanding”: three. “the spirit of counsel”: four. “And might”: five. “the spirit of knowledge”: six. “and of the fear of the Lord”: seven.

Those are the seven pillars of wisdom that Christ had. Seven represents completion, so they represent complete spiritual perfection, and that is what Christ operated in. Wisdom's house on seven pillars is Christ, full of the spirit of the Lord in every part.

thread.label: Proverbs 29:9
thread.text: If a wise man contendeth with a foolish man, whether he rage or laugh, there is no rest.

classes.title: Untruthful Trinity Revisited & Ridiculous

precepts.label: Sirach 33:5
precepts.why:
“If a wise man contendeth with a foolish man”: if a wise man debates with a stupid man or woman. And “whether he rage or laugh”: whether that fool laughs at it or is angry at it, “there is no rest.” There is no conclusion. It is a circular argument; you argue the same thing over and over again and it goes nowhere.

Sirach shows why: “The heart of the foolish is like a cartwheel; and his thoughts are like a rolling axletree.” The fool is a circular idiot. His mind just goes in circles, nonstop. That is the Trinity man: three is one, one is three, they are all the same, the Father and the Son of one substance. Round and round, and you cannot win. They are dead set in it, their minds sealed as with a hot iron.

Show them that the Father has sons, the children of Israel, and they cannot understand it: no, they are all one. Stump them in a debate and they keep going: but what about this? It is ongoing. It is a cartwheel. They will not yield to reason. Even the German had some sense when he called insanity doing the same thing over and over again and expecting different results.

So leave that negro alone. You are wasting your time. These are unreasonable people, and you have to let them go. The wise man who keeps contending with the fool gets no rest, because the fool's heart only rolls in circles of nonsense.

thread.label: Ecclesiastes 8:9
thread.text: All this have I seen, and applied my heart unto every work that is done under the sun: there is a time wherein one man ruleth over another to his own hurt.

classes.title: The Colossians & The CHRISTIANS of America

precepts.label: Zechariah 1:15
precepts.why:
“there is a time wherein one man ruleth over another to his own hurt.” That is Esau. The way Esau treated us is going to be to his own detriment.

The Lord says it in Zechariah: “And I am very sore displeased with the heathen that are at ease: for I was but a little displeased, and they helped forward the affliction.” Yes, we sinned against our God. Yes, the Lord allowed us to go into the hands of our enemies. But they took it too far.

God was but a little displeased with Israel, and the heathen helped forward the affliction. You think Christ ain't see that? That is why Esau's rule over Jacob is to his own hurt: he went past what God allowed, and the Lord is sore displeased with him for it.

precepts.label: Isaiah 63:9
precepts.why:
“In all their affliction he was afflicted, and the angel of his presence saved them”. In all of our affliction, through all of our slavery, the Lord saw all of it.

In all our affliction he was afflicted. So when he comes back, he is going to feel all of that pain and all of that suffering they did to the children of Israel, and he is going to wreak havoc on these nations.

“the angel of his presence saved them”. Salvation is not for the oppressors. Salvation is for those who have been afflicted. The man that ruled over another did it to his own hurt, because the one he afflicted is the one the Lord saves.

precepts.label: Psalms 119:85
precepts.why:
“The proud have digged pits for me, which are not after thy law.” The proud have digged pits for God's people.

They are not after God's laws. Look at it: how come you can abort in America? How come gay marriage is legalized? They don't keep God's laws and they don't uphold God's laws, but a lot of you coons out there follow behind this white man. They are not after God's commandments.

And who are the proud? Obadiah answers: it is Edom. The man that rules over another in Ecclesiastes 8 is the same proud one digging pits for Jacob, and his own pit is where he is headed.

precepts.label: Obadiah 1:1-3
precepts.why:
Who are the proud that digged the pits? “The pride of thine heart hath deceived thee, thou that dwellest in the clefts of the rock, whose habitation is high; that saith in his heart, Who shall bring me down to the ground?”

And who is he speaking to? Verse 1: “The vision of Obadiah. Thus saith the Lord God concerning Edom”. Concerning Edom: Esau, your friendly neighborhood white man, your Europeans, and the Americans.

Edom's pride has deceived him into thinking none shall bring him down. That is the one man who rules over another, and Solomon says he does it “to his own hurt.”

precepts.label: Ecclesiasticus 27:26-29
precepts.why:
“Whoso diggeth a pit shall fall therein: and he that setteth a trap shall be taken therein.” The proud digged pits for us, and they will fall in them. They thought evil against us, but the Lord saw it for good. Jacob is going to win in the end.

“He that worketh mischief, it shall fall upon him, and he shall not know whence it cometh.” That is what they do: they work mischief and call it law. And he is not going to know where it came from, because his pride has deceived him.

“Mockery and reproach are from the proud”. That is all they do: they accuse us, falsely accuse us, and mock us. “but vengeance, as a lion, shall lie in wait for them.” That lion is the one in Jeremiah 4:7.

“They that rejoice at the fall of the righteous shall be taken in the snare; and anguish shall consume them before they die.” Remember when they said raze it, raze it to the ground? The Lord has not forgotten. They will be taken in the snare. It does not pay to be wicked, and it does not pay to follow after your oppressor, because in the end they are going to be destroyed.

precepts.label: Psalms 94:20
precepts.why:
He that worketh mischief: that is what they do. “Shall the throne of iniquity have fellowship with thee, which frameth mischief by a law?” They work mischief and then call it law.

Two men getting married, two women getting married: all of these laws. Think about what Trump has done since he came into office: all of the firing and all the DEI hires, all of this is against us. They frame mischief and call it law.

A throne of iniquity cannot have fellowship with God. The ruler that frames mischief by a law over another man is ruling to his own hurt, and the mischief he works shall fall upon him.

precepts.label: Jeremiah 4:7
precepts.why:
Sirach said vengeance, as a lion, shall lie in wait for the proud. Jeremiah shows the lion: “The lion is come up from his thicket, and the destroyer of the Gentiles is on his way; he is gone forth from his place to make thy land desolate; and thy cities shall be laid waste, without an inhabitant.”

The destroyer of the Gentiles is on his way, to make the land desolate, without an inhabitant.

And that is twofold. It is talking about Nebuchadnezzar, and it is talking about Christ. The lion that came up against the land in the days of Jeremiah is a picture of the Lion that is coming for the nations that ruled over Israel to their own hurt.

precepts.label: Isaiah 26:10-14
precepts.why:
“Let favour be shewed to the wicked, yet will he not learn righteousness”. If favour was shown to Esau, he still wouldn't change his wicked ways. It does not pay to be wicked.

“in the land of uprightness will he deal unjustly, and will not behold the majesty of the Lord.” Where is the land of uprightness? The land of Israel. And what did he do there? He stole it. He will not behold the majesty of the Lord: he changes his image to a white man with stringy blonde hair and blue eyes.

“Lord, when thy hand is lifted up, they will not see: but they shall see, and be ashamed for their envy at the people”. The people are God's chosen people, the ones the heathen envy in 2 Esdras 2:28. “yea, the fire of thine enemies shall devour them. Lord, thou wilt ordain peace for us”, like we read earlier in Ephesians 2: he is going to ordain peace for us and destruction for our enemies.

“O Lord our God, other lords beside thee have had dominion over us”: like the so-called white man, like the Babylonians, like the Assyrians. “but by thee only will we make mention of thy name. They are dead, they shall not live; they are deceased, they shall not rise: therefore hast thou visited and destroyed them, and made all their memory to perish.” All of our enemies, all of these other lords that had rule over us, are dead. That is the hurt of the man that ruled over another.

precepts.label: 2 Esdras 2:28
precepts.why:
Isaiah said the wicked shall see and be ashamed for their envy at the people. Who are those people? God's chosen people. Ezra says it: “The heathen shall envy thee, but they shall be able to do nothing against thee, saith the Lord.”

The heathen shall envy the Israelites. But they shall be able to do nothing. They can't stop it, because they ain't going to be in rulership any more. They are not going to have ownership any more.

That is the end of the man who ruleth over another to his own hurt: the time of his rule runs out, and all his envy cannot stop what the Lord has spoken for Israel.

thread.label: Ecclesiastes 12:13
thread.text: Let us hear the conclusion of the whole matter: Fear God, and keep his commandments: for this is the whole duty of man.

classes.title: Transforming from Immorality into Beautiful Civility Part 2

precepts.label: Romans 8:19
precepts.why:
“Fear God, and keep his commandments: for this is the whole duty of man.” Man was put on this earth to rule it with God's commandments, and because we are not doing that, the earth is suffering; we are not in power. The earth was made to receive your direction, men.

Paul shows it: “For the earnest expectation of the creature waiteth for the manifestation of the sons of God.” Expectation means I am expecting something, and earnestly means with a begging type of attitude. The creation is earnestly waiting for the manifestation, and manifestation means the growth: time for us to stop being kids and manifest into men, to get ourselves together. The earth is waiting for the sons of God to manifest into gods, that is, to rule this planet properly.

And righteous women are waiting for that too. The woman is called woman because she is of man, and she is like the earth: you plant your seed in her and she brings forth fruit, but she needs your guidance. She is supposed to revolve around you, and when you are not in rulership she is out of orbit, like a satellite floating in space with no direction. That is why women cry, where are our black men? The father figure in the house got destroyed.

All of it fell apart when we broke the laws of the Most High from the very beginning, when the woman was out of order with her husband. So it is up to us men to fulfil the duty of manhood to fix it: to marry, build a nation, and rule rightly. That is what the whole creation is waiting on.

precepts.label: Ecclesiastes 12:14
precepts.why:
Verse 13 gives the whole duty of man; verse 14 gives the reason: “For God shall bring every work into judgment, with every secret thing, whether it be good, or whether it be evil.” For means because. Keep his commandments, because this is the whole reason God put man on the earth, and because God shall bring every work into judgment.

So if we are not dealing with our marriages properly, there is going to be a judgment for that, and we are looking at it. People try to figure out the problem in the black community: the marriages are messed up. Whoring, adultery, fornication. A little leaven will destroy the whole congregation, and it has to be rooted out like a cancer.

“with every secret thing”: the nasty stuff people do behind closed doors, thinking nobody sees. In nearly 35 years in this truth, we have seen the Most High bring out what people thought they could hide, and he brings it out at the worst time for you. Like applying for a job years later, thinking you got away with it, and they pull records you didn't know existed: get out of my office. That's how the Lord is.

So keep your slate clean. Be a disciplined man: you may not always be motivated, but you must always be disciplined. When sin comes before you, it stops right there. Because every work, good or evil, is going to come out, we have to be men of holiness, integrity, righteousness, dignity, honor and valor. That is the whole duty of man.

precepts.label: Ecclesiastes 10:20
precepts.why:
God shall bring every secret thing into judgment, and the Lord even calls a bird to bring it out: “Curse not the king, no not in thy thought; and curse not the rich in thy bedchamber: for a bird of the air shall carry the voice, and that which hath wings shall tell the matter.” We have sat in judgments where they asked, how did he find out? It's that damn bird. Somebody might think it's a literal bird flying around; I took every precaution. But the Most High is going to bring it out anyway. That's why it says every secret thing.

No, not in thy thought. Some people speak against the council and the leadership, or have evil thoughts against the leaders, and think they will get away with it. The Most High put leadership to watch over you, and that is not an easy job. Leaders must give an account, good or bad. The goal is to give a good account: the brother came in one way and now he is a man of valor, married, moving in the right direction; the sister listened to counsel and got herself together. When they will not take counsel, the leader still has to give an account, with grief.

This is how we should have grown up. We grew up in a lawless society; in slavery the fathers were stripped from the homes and the men forced to give their seed but not allowed to raise it. The matter will be told on you in your evil, so fear God, keep his commandments, and honor the ones set over you.

thread.label: Isaiah 1:4
thread.text: Ah sinful nation, a people laden with iniquity, a seed of evildoers, children that are corrupters: they have forsaken the Lord, they have provoked the Holy One of Israel unto anger, they are gone away backward.

classes.title: 70 Times 7: The Perfection of Mercy Through Christ

precepts.label: Matthew 11:28
precepts.why:
Isaiah calls us “a people laden with iniquity.” Christ answers that very word: “Come unto me, all ye that labour and are heavy laden, and I will give you rest.” Heavy laden with what? With sin, the iniquity Isaiah just named.

That is why we are in need of a saviour. We read the history of our forefathers in the wilderness: the Most High showed great signs and wonders, and we were still a stiff-necked, hard-headed people. We are “a sinful nation”, “a seed of evildoers, children that are corrupters.” We forsake the Lord every time we sin, and we have “provoked the Holy One of Israel unto anger.” That is why the so-called blacks and Hispanics went into captivity, just as Deuteronomy 28:15 through 68 laid out the curses for breaking the commandments. Many of our brothers and sisters are still going backward, moonwalking away from the Most High. Brothers and sisters, we cannot do it without Christ.

So be honest and sincere, even in prayer. Do not go to the Most High acting righteous when you are full of dead bones, sin and guile. None of us is righteous; we are trying, but there is sin still in us. Open your mouth and confess the things you are battling with.

“and I will give you rest.” That rest is not a good night’s sleep. It is our land, the kingdom of God, rulership for a thousand years under Christ. That is the true rest he is talking about, but we have to come unto him. Now is our time to get our minds right and repent.

thread.label: Isaiah 8:1-4
thread.text: Moreover the Lord said unto me, Take thee a great roll, and write in it with a man’s pen concerning Maher–shalal–hash–baz.

classes.title: The Nativity: the Bloodline, Birthright, & the Messiah

precepts.label: Isaiah 8:18
precepts.why:
Isaiah had just told Ahaz, “the Lord himself shall give you a sign”. Then in chapter 8 the Lord has Isaiah write the name Maher-shalal-hash-baz, quick to the plunder, swift to the spoil, and Isaiah goes unto the prophetess, his wife, and “she conceived, and bare a son.” The child was named before he was conceived, the same way Gabriel named John and named Christ before they were conceived.

Then Isaiah says who the sign is: “Behold, I and the children whom the Lord hath given me are for signs and for wonders in Israel from the Lord of hosts, which dwelleth in mount Zion.” Behold who? I, Isaiah, and the children. Not his wife. He never counts the woman.

So the sign of Isaiah 7:14 was not the virgin; it was the child. The virgin birth was garbage. The birth of Isaiah's son was the sign that Ephraim and Syria banding together against Judah would fail. Before the child could cry “My father, and my mother,” the riches of Damascus and the spoil of Samaria were taken away before the king of Assyria. Assyria would pass through Judah and “reach even to the neck”, coming close to conquering but failing, because of Immanuel: “Take counsel together, and it shall come to nought; speak the word, and it shall not stand: for God is with us.” Once Isaiah's son was born, the two kings could not succeed against Judah.

precepts.label: Ezekiel 12:6
precepts.why:
The Lord told Ezekiel to bear his stuff on his shoulders in their sight and carry it forth in the twilight, covering his face “that thou see not the ground: for I have set thee for a sign unto the house of Israel.” God made Ezekiel himself a sign unto the house of Israel.

Read on to verse 11 and Ezekiel is told to say it to Israel plainly: “Say, I am your sign: like as I have done, so shall it be done unto them: they shall remove and go into captivity.” What the prophet did, Israel would go through.

This lines up with Isaiah 8. When the Lord gives a sign, it is the man and the child he gives, not the woman. Isaiah and his children were signs and wonders in Israel, and Ezekiel was set for a sign to the house of Israel, which is why the sign of Isaiah 7:14 is the child born to Isaiah and the prophetess.

precepts.label: Ezekiel 24:24
precepts.why:
“Thus Ezekiel is unto you a sign.” What is he? A sign. Not his wife: Ezekiel. “according to all that he hath done shall ye do: and when this cometh, ye shall know that I am the Lord God.”

The Lord told Ezekiel to eat dung, and what did we end up doing? Eating dung. He was a sign, and what he did came upon Israel.

Read on to verse 27: “thou shalt be a sign unto them; and they shall know that I am the Lord.” Again and again the man is the sign. So when Isaiah says “I and the children whom the Lord hath given me are for signs”, it fits the pattern of the prophets: the sign given to Ahaz was the child Isaiah's wife bare, Maher-shalal-hash-baz, not a virgin.

precepts.label: Luke 11:29-30
precepts.why:
When the people were gathered thick together, Christ said, “This is an evil generation: they seek a sign; and there shall no sign be given it, but the sign of Jonas the prophet.” Then: “For as Jonas was a sign unto the Ninevites, so shall also the Son of man be to this generation.”

Jonas was a sign. The Son of man was a sign. Men were always the signs. There is no scripture where the women were signs. Hosea was also a sign, and his marriage was a sign, but the woman by herself was never a sign.

That settles Isaiah 7 and 8. The Lord said he would give Ahaz a sign, and Isaiah tells us who it was: himself and the children the Lord gave him. The son born to Isaiah and the prophetess was the sign that God was with Judah, Immanuel, and that the two kings coming against Judah would come to nought.

thread.label: Isaiah 9:16
thread.text: For the leaders of this people cause them to err; and they that are led of them are destroyed.

classes.title: There Is No Hate Like Christian Love

precepts.label: Hosea 8:3-4
precepts.why:
“For the leaders of this people cause them to err; and they that are led of them are destroyed.” Who are the leaders in the Black community today? Your Black leaders have you fighting for Palestinians and fighting all kinds of stupid battles. And you Black Christians that are led of them are destroyed. Our people are so destroyed they don't even know it: destroyed with a warm fuzzy feeling every Sunday. The pastors are the new taskmasters. They get sent out by Esau, they learned the doctrines from Esau, and they bring it into your community, pulling up in the Benz while you walk to church in the cold and give him your last.

Hosea shows how it came to this. “Israel hath cast off the thing that is good: the enemy shall pursue him.” What is good? The laws of God, this Bible. Israel cast them off, and because of that the enemy pursues him.

“They have set up kings, but not by me: they have made princes, and I knew it not.” You set up leaders, brothers and sisters, but it isn't of the Lord. “Of their silver and their gold have they made them idols, that they may be cut off.” You make these men, these so-called leaders, your idols. You follow them wholeheartedly. Pastor says he needs an extra thousand dollars and you say, Pastor, I'mma work it out, I'mma get you your money. That's cold pimping.

And look at the fruit: a grandmother in Jamal Bryant's church sowing her twelve hundred dollars and being embarrassed because it was not enough; Eddie Long on the throne while the white man holds the mic and tells him he is no longer a commoner. These are your leaders that cause you to err.

“That they may be cut off.” And now we are cut off. That is what comes of casting off the law of God and setting up kings the Lord never chose.

precepts.label: Proverbs 3:31
precepts.why:
“Envy thou not the oppressor, and choose none of his ways.” Put the oppressors on the screen: Pope Nicholas V and Pope Alexander VI. In 1452 Pope Nicholas V issued Dum Diversas, authorizing King Alfonso V of Portugal to fight, subjugate and conquer the Saracens and pagans in African territory. Those were good Christians.

Think about it. Without those two devils, those two Christians, there would be no such thing as an African-American, a Jamaican, a Haitian, a Puerto Rican. We are named after whatever landmass we were scattered to, and we are the result of those men. Christians did this to us. And now we revel in it, reverence them, and follow their laws and their ways of life.

The scripture says choose none of his ways. But tomorrow at 11 o'clock Sunday morning, where will all our people be? Not listening to the truth. They will be in church getting a good dose of the doctrine of the man that enslaved them, that turned them into African-Americans and Jamaicans and Haitians. They can't wait to go learn about a good Jesus.

That is the leaders of Isaiah 9:16 causing our people to err. Look at the results of being taught Christianity: a man on television saying he is a Christian first and that black is a construct, when the white man put us in chains and did not do that to his own people; a girl who let a boy call her the N-word and call him master; our people turning up on each other and showing teeth to everybody else. That is what comes of envying the oppressor and choosing his ways.

precepts.label: Mark 8:36-37
precepts.why:
Terence Crawford said there was not a number that could get him back in that ring, and then said for 100 million dollars you can have my soul. That nigger was dead serious; look at his eyes. That is a dangerous man: a man who would sell out his mama and his children and do anything for money. That is the result of 400 years with Esau, and he just said out loud what the majority of Black celebrities, rappers and singers think.

“For what shall it profit a man, if he shall gain the whole world, and lose his own soul?” Esau gives you whatever you want: all the riches, all the connections, all the power, wealth you can't run from. But in order to get it, you lose your own soul.

“Or what shall a man give in exchange for his soul?” What do these celebrities give in exchange for their souls? Their booty. They give it up, and Amalek takes it. Your Jay-Zs and 50 Cents, your Mariah Careys and Whitneys: they have to give in order to receive.

What are you going to stand for if everything is about money? You have no dignity and no morals. These are the results of the leaders of this people causing them to err, and of Black Christians led by them being destroyed. There are no laws with them, because they were taught the laws are done away with.

thread.label: Isaiah 11:1-4
thread.text: And there shall come forth a rod out of the stem of Jesse, and a Branch shall grow out of his roots:

classes.title: Stay in the Spirit

precepts.label: 1 Corinthians 1:24
precepts.why:
“And there shall come forth a rod out of the stem of Jesse, and a Branch shall grow out of his roots: And the spirit of the Lord shall rest upon him, the spirit of wisdom and understanding.” Who is that stem coming out of Jesse? Christ. The spirit of the Lord rests upon Christ; the spirit of wisdom and understanding rests upon Christ. Paul says it plainly: “But unto them which are called, both Jews and Greeks, Christ the power of God, and the wisdom of God.”

Christ is the wisdom of God. And wisdom makes all things new. That is why 2 Corinthians 5:17 says, “Therefore if any man be in Christ, he is a new creature”: any man in Christ is a new creature because the power and the wisdom of God makes all things new.

Isaiah shows what is contained in the Holy Spirit that rested on him: “the spirit of wisdom and understanding, the spirit of counsel and might, the spirit of knowledge and of the fear of the Lord.” It made him “of quick understanding in the fear of the Lord”, the way King Solomon said he was a witty child, and the way John leaped in Elizabeth’s womb when Mary visited: there is a spirit in the womb.

Christ is also the power of God, and Isaiah shows that power too: “he shall smite the earth with the rod of his mouth, and with the breath of his lips shall he slay the wicked.” And when you have that spirit, you will not judge after the sight of your eyes; “with righteousness shall he judge the poor, and reprove with equity for the meek of the earth.” Reproving with equity means you are not partial. With the spirit of the Lord you are not going to be in partiality; you will have knowledge and understanding, and you will obtain the wisdom, retain it and apply it.

thread.label: Isaiah 14:1-2
thread.text: For the Lord will have mercy on Jacob, and will yet choose Israel, and set them in their own land: and the strangers shall be joined with them, and they shall cleave to the house of Jacob.

classes.title: The Colossians & The CHRISTIANS of America

thread.label: Isaiah 14:3-4
thread.text: And it shall come to pass in the day that the Lord shall give thee rest from thy sorrow, and from thy fear, and from the hard bondage wherein thou wast made to serve,

classes.title: Lucifer: The Antichrist

precepts.label: Revelation 18:10
precepts.why:
“That thou shalt take up this proverb against the king of Babylon, and say, How hath the oppressor ceased! the golden city ceased!” In the day the Lord gives us rest from our sorrow, our fear and the hard bondage we were made to serve in, we are going to be speaking against America. The king of Babylon here is America, and this is how we know Lucifer is not an angel: Lucifer is called the king of Babylon, the oppressor, the golden city. In Revelation it is mystery Babylon the great, and Revelation 18 explains that city.

“Standing afar off for the fear of her torment, saying, Alas, alas, that great city Babylon, that mighty city! for in one hour is thy judgment come.” Remember what we read in Isaiah 14: the king of Babylon. Here it is that great city Babylon, that mighty city, and her judgment comes in one hour.

So Lucifer is a city, a country, rulers, a government. “The Lord hath broken the staff of the wicked, and the sceptre of the rulers.” It is not talking about a fallen angel; it is talking about America, the king of Babylon, whose ceasing Israel will proclaim when the Lord gives us rest from the hard bondage.

precepts.label: Revelation 18:17
precepts.why:
Isaiah calls the king of Babylon “the golden city”: “How hath the oppressor ceased! the golden city ceased!” Why does it say golden city? Revelation 18 explains it: “For in one hour so great riches is come to nought.”

So great riches: that is the golden city. It is called golden because America is rich. Lucifer is talking about America. And all those riches come to nothing in one hour, the same hour of judgment in verse 10, when they stand afar off crying, “Alas, alas, that great city Babylon, that mighty city!”

The golden city ceasing in Isaiah is the great riches coming to nought in Revelation. It is not an angel that falls; it is a rich nation, a government, the oppressor that made us serve in hard bondage, and in the day the Lord gives us rest, we will take up this proverb against it.

precepts.label: Lamentations 2:1
precepts.why:
“How art thou fallen from heaven, O Lucifer, son of the morning! how art thou cut down to the ground.” Who is Lucifer, and what heaven did he fall from? When it says fall from heaven, it is not talking about literal heaven. In the scriptures there are the heavens where the Lord is, which is paradise; there is heaven that is the sky and space; and there are heavens that are a place of authority. Lamentations shows that last one.

“How hath the Lord covered the daughter of Zion with a cloud in his anger, and cast down from heaven unto the earth the beauty of Israel.” The beauty of Israel was cast down from heaven to the earth. That means we were brought down low: brought into captivity, no longer on top, no longer ruling. It is a good analogy showing that heaven also goes into rulership.

So Lucifer falling from heaven is a ruler falling from his place of authority, not an angel falling out of the sky. Read on in Isaiah 14 and he is named: Israel will “take up this proverb against the king of Babylon, and say, How hath the oppressor ceased! the golden city ceased!” Lucifer is the king of Babylon, the oppressor, the golden city, because America is rich. And “They that see thee shall narrowly look upon thee, and consider thee, saying, Is this the man that made the earth to tremble, that did shake kingdoms”: Lucifer is a man, the man of sin, the fourth beast, the white man.

The same Lord who cast Israel down from heaven to the earth will cut this ruler down to the ground. It is a future prophecy of America being destroyed.

precepts.label: Isaiah 13:19
precepts.why:
“How art thou fallen from heaven, O Lucifer, son of the morning! how art thou cut down to the ground, which didst weaken the nations!” Lucifer is another name for Esau, alongside Tyrus and Edom, and further up the chapter he is called the king of Babylon. How did he weaken the nations? Through war. A US destroyer took down two fighter jets in ninety-three seconds, having calculated seventeen ways to kill them before they reached altitude. Venezuela’s defenses, its bases and its president were taken in thirty minutes. That is why his pride is lifted up, and why the ignorant say he must be God.

Isaiah 13 names what he is: “And Babylon, the glory of kingdoms.” The Space Command headquarters moving to Huntsville, Alabama, now to be called Rocket City, means more weaponry, the smith and the waster that God created. Babylon is the glory of kingdoms: all these nations want to come to Babylon and get a piece of it. They call it the American dream.

The world is amazed at the beast: “Who is like unto the beast? who is able to make war with him?” But that same verse of Isaiah 13 says the glory of kingdoms shall be as when God overthrew Sodom and Gomorrah. The Lord “hath broken the staff of the wicked, and the sceptre of the rulers. He who smote the people in wrath with a continual stroke”, primarily God’s people, is brought down.

So the glory of kingdoms falls from heaven like Lucifer, and then “The whole earth is at rest, and is quiet: they break forth into singing.” When these devils fall, the whole earth will finally be at rest.

precepts.label: Revelation 11:8
precepts.why:
“The burden of Egypt. Behold, the Lord rideth upon a swift cloud, and shall come into Egypt: and the idols of Egypt shall be moved at his presence.” The commentaries say this is about ancient times, but verse 1 lets you know it is future: the Lord coming into Egypt has not happened yet. So how do we know who this Egypt is?

Revelation tells us: “And their dead bodies shall lie in the street of the great city, which spiritually is called Sodom and Egypt, where also our Lord was crucified.” The dead bodies are the Israelites, not literally dead but spiritually dead. The great city is Babylon the great, the United States of America. “which spiritually”: that is the key.

It is called Sodom because of the same-sex marriages, the transgenderism and all that filth in this country. It is not the real Sodom but a spiritual Sodom. And it is called Egypt: America knows its foundation is ancient Egypt. Look at the dollar bill: the pyramid, the all-seeing eye of Horus, 1776 at the bottom, Novus Ordo Seclorum, the New World Order, and the obelisk in Washington DC. America is aware that this is a spiritual Egypt; only the black and Latin Christians have not figured it out, and so they read the scriptures desperately confused.

“where also our Lord was crucified.” Christ was crucified in Jerusalem, but this is a spiritual crucifixion: they have crucified Christ’s image here and crucified his teachings here.

So Isaiah 19 is spiritual Egypt: “And I will set the Egyptians against the Egyptians: and they shall fight every one against his brother, and every one against his neighbour; city against city, and kingdom against kingdom.” Americans against Americans, a house divided: Democrats against Republicans, red cities against blue cities, white man against white man. There will be a civil war in this country.

thread.label: Isaiah 19:2
thread.text: And I will set the Egyptians against the Egyptians: and they shall fight every one against his brother, and every one against his neighbour; city against city, and kingdom against kingdom.
