precepts.label: Isaiah 31:3
precepts.why:
“Now the Egyptians are men, and not God; and their horses flesh, and not spirit.” That is the war of gods. On one side is the god still sitting in our minds, the image of white supremacy that was forced into our spirits; on the other side is the God of this Bible. The Egyptians set themselves up as gods, but they are only men, and all their weaponry is flesh.

Their weapons are not only for warring with other people. They are there to force a thought into our minds, to force white supremacy into our spirits. So the war is first in the mind, and the ignorance of our people is the battlefield.

“When the Lord shall stretch out his hand, both he that helpeth shall fall, and he that is holpen shall fall down, and they all shall fail together.” That is what Isaiah 19 shows: the Lord sets “the Egyptians against the Egyptians”, “city against city, and kingdom against kingdom”, and “the spirit of Egypt shall fail in the midst thereof.” There is going to be civil war, and there will be wars from outside as well.

And when it comes, “they shall seek to the idols, and to the charmers, and to them that have familiar spirits, and to the wizards.” They will cry out to the images they revered as gods, talking to those Jesus pieces, asking them to come save them. They will run back to the news outlets that lied for years, to Christianity, to every version of white supremacy. But men are not God, and none of it will hold them up.

So the Lord is teaching us war tactics, because there are going to be wars in the flesh. We have to keep strong in the war we already have in our spirit, knowing the ones who made themselves gods over us are only flesh.

precepts.label: Revelation 11:8
precepts.why:
Revelation 11 shows everybody where Egypt is: “their dead bodies shall lie in the street of the great city, which spiritually is called Sodom and Egypt, where also our Lord was crucified.” This place, America, is spiritually called Sodom and Egypt. So when Isaiah says “I will set the Egyptians against the Egyptians”, he is speaking of civil war in this land, city against city and kingdom against kingdom.

That is why Isaiah 19 goes on: “The Lord hath mingled a perverse spirit in the midst thereof: and they have caused Egypt to err in every work thereof.” God put a perverse spirit here, and it causes this place to be in error in everything it does. Everything that America does is in error, because there is a perverse spirit here.

You can see it in the news. Trump went to the Ford plant, a worker called him a pedophile protector, and he shot the man the bird and said “F you”. The man was suspended, and the union is fighting to get him off suspension. Somebody called out the perverse spirit, and even when they are shown their errors, they flip you the bird and make sure you lose your job.

So Sodom and Egypt is not a far-off place. It is the land we are in, and the land that the Lord will turn against itself.

thread.text: Whom the Lord of hosts shall bless, saying, Blessed be Egypt my people, and Assyria the work of my hands, and Israel mine inheritance.

precepts.label: Isaiah 27:12-13
precepts.why:
“Blessed be Egypt my people, and Assyria the work of my hands, and Israel mine inheritance.” That is the one verse they might run with: see, Egypt is his people and Assyria is his people, so the Egyptians and the Assyrians are saved too. No problem. Go over a few chapters and see where this Egypt and Assyria are.

“And it shall come to pass in that day, that the Lord shall beat off from the channel of the river unto the stream of Egypt, and ye shall be gathered one by one, O ye children of Israel.” Gathered one by one: who? The children of Israel.

“And it shall come to pass in that day, that the great trumpet shall be blown”: that is Christ coming. “And they shall come which were ready to perish in the land of Assyria, and the outcasts in the land of Egypt.” Earlier it said Egypt and Assyria; here it is the land of Assyria and the land of Egypt, and the ones coming out of them are the children of Israel. So who is “Egypt my people” and Assyria? Israelites.

“And shall worship the Lord in the holy mount at Jerusalem.” My people in Egypt and my people in Assyria means Israel in those lands, scattered there and gathered out one by one to worship at Jerusalem. That is how precepts work: you don't build a doctrine for another nation on one verse.

precepts.label: Isaiah 11:11
precepts.why:
Just in case Isaiah 27 is not enough, beat a dead horse. “And it shall come to pass in that day, that the Lord shall set his hand again the second time to recover the remnant of his people.” That is the same gathering we read in Isaiah 27.

From where? “Which shall be left, from Assyria”: my people. “And from Egypt”: Egypt, my people. “And from Pathros”: still Egypt, my people. “And from Cush, and from Elam”: Elam is Iran and Pakistan, my people. “And from Shinar”: Shinar is Iraq, my people. “And from Hamath”: Syria, my people. “And from the islands of the sea”: the islands, whether the Mediterranean or the Caribbean. That is his people.

It names Assyria and Egypt right there with the rest, and in every one of those places it is the remnant of his people that he recovers, not the nations of those lands. So when Isaiah 19 says “Blessed be Egypt my people, and Assyria the work of my hands”, it is speaking of Israel scattered in Egypt and Assyria, whom the Lord recovers the second time.

precepts.label: Zechariah 10:6-10
precepts.why:
One more, just in case. “And I will strengthen the house of Judah, and I will save the house of Joseph, and I will bring them again to place them.” Bring them again: that is the second time, the recovering of Isaiah 11. “For I have mercy upon them: and they shall be as though I had not cast them off”: as though they had never been in captivity. “For I am the Lord their God, and will hear them.”

“And they of Ephraim shall be like a mighty man, and their heart shall rejoice as through wine: yea, their children shall see it, and be glad.” “I will hiss for them, and gather them; for I have redeemed them.” Both Judah and Joseph, Judah and Ephraim: he will gather all twelve tribes. “And they shall increase as they have increased. And I will sow them among the people: and they shall remember me in far countries; and they shall live with their children, and turn again.”

“I will bring them again also out of the land of Egypt, and gather them out of Assyria.” Bring who again? All twelve tribes, out of Egypt and out of Assyria, the same as Isaiah 11:11. “And I will bring them into the land of Gilead and Lebanon; and place shall not be found for them.”

So what does “Egypt my people” and “Assyria the work of my hands” mean? It means Israel in those lands. That makes four scriptures, and there is no arguing with it. That is called precepts.

precepts.label: Exodus 15:3
precepts.why:
In Isaiah 45 the Lord says, “For Jacob my servant’s sake, and Israel mine elect, I have even called thee by thy name: I have surnamed thee, though thou hast not known me”. God surnamed us, and even though he revealed himself to us and delivered us numerous times, we kept turning our backs on him. “I am the Lord, and there is none else, there is no God beside me”. Some set themselves up as gods, and some create gods in their minds and as idols, but there is none with him. “I form the light, and create darkness: I make peace, and create evil: I the Lord do all these things”.

Exodus 15:3 fills in the picture: “The Lord is a man of war: the Lord is his name”. The same Lord that forms the light, creates darkness, makes peace and creates evil is also a man of war. That is the overall picture of the Lord our God.

Psalms 46 shows what that looks like: “Come, behold the works of the Lord, what desolations he hath made in the earth”. Pharaohs were worshipped as gods, Xerxes thought he was a god, and Antiochus Epiphanes thought he was God manifest on earth; rulers rise in power and rise in pride. But “He maketh wars to cease unto the end of the earth; he breaketh the bow, and cutteth the spear in sunder”. The man on the thumbnail who has claimed for two years that he will stop the war between Ukraine and Russia has not stopped anything. When the Iron Dome in Israel failed and the rockets came through, that was no technical glitch; the Lord ripped it open. He makes the prideful instruments of man fail, because he decides where war happens and when it ceases.

And that God of war, who formed the light and created darkness, is Christ. He is our refuge, and he teaches his soldiers to do the same: “Blessed be the Lord my strength, which teacheth my hands to war, and my fingers to fight”. He handpicked us to be soldiers in his army.

thread.label: Isaiah 47:1
thread.text: Come down, and sit in the dust, O virgin daughter of Babylon, sit on the ground: there is no throne, O daughter of the Chaldeans: for thou shalt no more be called tender and delicate.

classes.title: Christ: the Enemy of Christianity
Transforming from Immorality into Beautiful Civility Part 2

precepts.label: Psalms 137:7
precepts.why:
Who is the virgin daughter of Babylon? Let's identify her. “Remember, O Lord, the children of Edom in the day of Jerusalem; who said, Rase it, rase it, even to the foundation thereof.” Destroy it, destroy it. Then, speaking to the same people: “O daughter of Babylon, who art to be destroyed”. Edom is now called the daughter of Babylon, and she is destined to be destroyed.

So Isaiah 47 is the destruction of Babylon, which is Edom, the very thing David said in the psalm. “Come down, and sit in the dust, O virgin daughter of Babylon, sit on the ground”: you have been taken down, defeated. Then “there is no throne”: your throne is finished, your throne is over.

Then, “for thou shalt no more be called tender and delicate.” Babylon calls herself tender and delicate. How? The United States of America says, we are a Christian nation. She has two horns like a lamb, Republicans and Democrats, and says, we are Christian, in God we trust. That is the tender and delicate virgin, and God says she will be called that no more.

The children of Edom who cried to raze Jerusalem to its foundation are the daughter of Babylon today, America, and she is the one who is to be destroyed.

precepts.label: Judges 16:21
precepts.why:
Isaiah tells the daughter of Babylon, “Take the millstones, and grind meal”. What does that mean? When you take millstones and grind meal, you are working. But what kind of work? Look at what happened to Samson.

Samson listened to that woman called Delilah, who got paid to take his strength and destroy this mighty black man. She was a black woman, not an Israelite but a Hamite, a good-looking Hamite, and she gave it to him so good that he told her his secrets and went to sleep on her knees. The Philistines came in, cut his hair, bound him up and took his eyes out: “But the Philistines took him, and put out his eyes, and brought him down to Gaza, and bound him with fetters of brass; and he did grind in the prison house.”

When it says they made him grind, they made him work. That is slavery. Even when you go to prison they make you work, and that is still slavery: look up the 13th Amendment.

So this is what God is saying to America, to these Europeans, these Caucasians: take the millstones and grind meal. Get ready for slavery. Then “uncover thy locks, make bare the leg, uncover the thigh, pass over the rivers.” As a tender and delicate virgin her head was covered; God says uncover it, lift the dress to the calf, then to the thigh. The rivers she passes over are the word of God, “the washing of water by the word”. America says, I am a virgin daughter, a Christian nation, and the prophets open the word of God and show she is not, revealing her wickedness.

precepts.label: Revelation 17:16
precepts.why:
“Thy nakedness shall be uncovered, yea, thy shame shall be seen: I will take vengeance, and I will not meet thee as a man.” How is America's nakedness uncovered? Through the prophets: the brothers on the streets, on YouTube, traveling, must uncover America's nakedness and reveal her wickedness. And Christ is not coming back as a man; he is coming back as God, because only a God can take down the United States of America. Russia can't do it, China can't do it. America has bases all over the world, and no other nation has that power.

Revelation 17 shows what happens to America and her allies: “And the ten horns which thou sawest upon the beast, these shall hate the whore, and shall make her desolate and naked, and shall eat her flesh, and burn her with fire.” The ten horns on the beast with seven heads are NATO, the EU. They shall hate America, make her desolate and naked, eat her flesh, and burn her with fire. That is the United States of America burnt up and destroyed.

Is America finished then? The party ain't over. 2 Esdras 15 says, “And in the passage they shall rush on the idle city, and shall destroy some portion of thy land, and consume part of thy glory, and shall return to Babylon that was destroyed.” Not all of her is destroyed in that war. The country as we know it is finished, but America is not down yet, with all those bases everywhere.

That is why Isaiah says “I will not meet thee as a man.” The ten horns can make her naked and burn her, but the only one that can finally destroy America is God, Christ when he returns.

precepts.label: Romans 9:17
precepts.why:
The only one that can destroy America is Christ when he returns, and Romans 9 shows why God raised her up at all: “For the scripture saith unto Pharaoh, Even for this same purpose have I raised thee up, that I might shew my power in thee, and that my name might be declared throughout all the earth.”

Pharaoh was over Egypt, and Egypt has long been destroyed. Pharaoh is a metaphor for Rome, and a metaphor for America today. Revelation calls the great city spiritually Sodom and Egypt, and that is Pharaoh right there.

God raised America up. Why? That he might show his power in her. All the technological advances America has, God allowed her to have. There is no nation, no country, that can match Babylon the Great; that is why they call it the great: it has the greatest technology of all nations. Christ says, I must show my power in you, because I am the only one that can take America out.

Then “and that my name might be declared throughout all the earth.” When Christ finally takes them down, his name shall be declared throughout all the earth, because we are going to declare his real name, his true name. That is the vengeance of Isaiah 47: “I will take vengeance, and I will not meet thee as a man.”

thread.label: Isaiah 47:6
thread.text: I was wroth with my people, I have polluted mine inheritance, and given them into thine hand: thou didst shew them no mercy; upon the ancient hast thou very heavily laid thy yoke.

classes.title: Christ: the Enemy of Christianity

precepts.label: Deuteronomy 28:48
precepts.why:
“I was wroth with my people”: wroth means angry. The pictures of our people in slavery, beaten, on the slave ships, lynched, murdered from the time of slavery all the way up to now, are God being wroth with his people. It is like a family album of our family. He allowed the white man to beat the hell out of us, and we were made slaves for the white man.

Deuteronomy 28:48 is what that anger looked like: “he shall put a yoke of iron upon thy neck, until he have destroyed thee.” Think about the mindset of the brother in those conditions, with the big yoke of iron on his neck and in the different positions of slavery. Your mind is going to go crazy, because you know you are not supposed to be in that situation. That is what those torture devices were set to do.

“until he have destroyed thee” means until your mind breaks down, until your manhood is gone and your ability to be free is gone. When you just succumb to being a slave, your mental strength and fortitude to be independent is broken. That is what black people are today.

So Isaiah 47:6 says the same: “thou didst shew them no mercy; upon the ancient hast thou very heavily laid thy yoke.” This Christian nation, as they say, showed us no mercy, and laid the yoke heavy even on the oldest among us. And she said “I shall be a lady for ever”, I will be Christian forever, and did not lay these things to heart, “neither didst remember the latter end of it”, though they have the Bible and know what it says will happen at the latter end.

precepts.label: Colossians 2:8
precepts.why:
“I have polluted mine inheritance.” How did God pollute his people? With man-made religions. Paul warns: “Beware lest any man spoil you through philosophy and vain deceit, after the tradition of men, after the rudiments of the world, and not after Christ.” None of these religions are after Christ.

Look at where they came from. Pope Nicholas V, the father of the transatlantic slave trade, and after the popes the Protestants. John Smith created the Baptist religion. Joseph Smith created the Mormon religion in 1830. Ellen G. White created the Seventh-day Adventist religion in 1863. Charles T. Russell created the Jehovah's Witness religion in 1872. Charles Parham created the Pentecostal religion in 1901.

These run from slavery up to 1863, when we so-called got emancipated, and on through Jim Crow and segregation. The same people who held us as slaves handed us these religions. What happened to John 3:16 and Galatians 3:28 while our people were in chains? They took that out of the Bible at that time.

So Isaiah 47:6 shows God allowed us to be polluted: “I was wroth with my people, I have polluted mine inheritance, and given them into thine hand.” The traditions of men that spoiled our people are part of that pollution, and that is why Christ is the enemy of Christianity.

thread.label: Isaiah 47:8
thread.text: Therefore hear now this, thou that art given to pleasures, that dwellest carelessly, that sayest in thine heart, I am, and none else beside me; I shall not sit as a widow, neither shall I know the loss of children:

classes.title: Christ: the Enemy of Christianity

precepts.label: Nahum 3:4
precepts.why:
“Therefore hear now this, thou that art given to pleasures, that dwellest carelessly.” Given to pleasures: Lifestyles of the Rich and Famous, champagne wishes and caviar dreams, and it made negroes jealous and envious. “that sayest in thine heart, I am, and none else beside me.” Only the Most High can say I am; they are setting themselves up as God on earth. “I shall not sit as a widow”: I will always have my allies. “neither shall I know the loss of children”: my citizens will not die. “But these two things shall come to thee in a moment in one day, the loss of children, and widowhood”: their citizens put to death, and their allies cutting them loose, “for the multitude of thy sorceries.” Their science and technology, like the mystery weapon that left Venezuelan soldiers bleeding through the nose, God calls witchcraft.

Nahum names her: “Because of the multitude of the whoredoms of the wellfavoured harlot, the mistress of witchcrafts, that selleth nations through her whoredoms, and families through her witchcrafts.” The well-favoured harlot is the same whore of Revelation 17, America, the same virgin daughter of Babylon. She is well-favoured because this is Babylon the great: everybody wants to come here; everybody says, I can get rich there.

precepts.why:
Ezekiel 35:12 says God has heard all Edom’s blasphemies: “I have heard all thy blasphemies which thou hast spoken against the mountains of Israel, saying, They are laid desolate, they are given us to consume.” Christ names that same blasphemy in Revelation: “I know the blasphemy of them which say they are Jews, and are not, but are the synagogue of Satan.”

That is the blasphemy: Edom took over the land and said, it is given to us, we are the Jews. They are not the Jews, and the land is not theirs. Revelation 3:9 says it again: “I will make them of the synagogue of Satan, which say they are Jews, and are not, but do lie”. They are the devil the Bible speaks of, and it is the Son of God who said it.

The verse also speaks to our people: “I know thy works, and tribulation, and poverty, (but thou art rich)”. That is our poverty, but we are rich, because we are the children of God.

“Thus with your mouth ye have boasted against me, and have multiplied your words against me: I have heard them.” By calling themselves Jews and claiming the land as Jews, Edom has boasted against God, and God heard every word. So “When the whole earth rejoiceth, I will make thee desolate”: when all creation is singing, Edom is destroyed. “As thou didst rejoice at the inheritance of the house of Israel, because it was desolate, so will I do unto thee: thou shalt be desolate, O mount Seir, and all Idumea, even all of it”.

Our people share in the blasphemy too. Ezekiel 36:20 says that when Israel was scattered among the heathen “they profaned my holy name, when they said to them, These are the people of the Lord, and are gone forth out of his land.” Every black and Latino Christian who points at the people in the land and says, those are the Jews, profanes God’s name. It was prophesied that the Messiah would come through Edom’s religion, Christianity, as a lord bent on doing away with all moral restraints: keep no commandments, keep no laws. That is the religion of Edom, and Christ is its enemy.

classes.title: Christ: the Enemy of Christianity

precepts.label: Ezekiel 36:19
precepts.why:
Ezekiel 36:5 says Idumea “appointed my land into their possession with the joy of all their heart, with despiteful minds, to cast it out for a prey.” They were happy to steal that land. With despiteful minds means they took it knowing, despite the fact, that it was not theirs and that they are not the Jews; they took it as the Jews and said God gave them that land. To cast it out for a prey means they called their fellow Europeans from Poland, from Czechoslovakia, from Germany, from Russia, from Uzbekistan: come and get some land. That is why you have all those funny-looking people over there. Their own scholars write that Edom means the Roman Empire and the European powers, Rome the Edomite capital, the Pope the head of the Edomite religion, and that religion is Christianity.

Then verse 19 shows how that could happen: “And I scattered them among the heathen, and they were dispersed through the countries: according to their way and according to their doings I judged them.” We were scattered amongst the heathen, dispersed through the countries, and God judged our people for our ways.

Read on: “And when they entered unto the heathen, whither they went, they profaned my holy name, when they said to them, These are the people of the Lord, and are gone forth out of his land.” Wherever we went, we profaned God's holy name. How? When we said to the heathen, these are the people of the Lord: those are the Jews. All Black Christians say that. All Latino Christians say that, pointing at Amalek in the land and calling them the Jews. That is how we profane God's name.

So Idumea sits in our land with despiteful minds, and our own people, scattered and judged, stand beside them and call them God's people. The land was taken by Edom, and the lie was confirmed by Israel in its Christianity.

precepts.label: Deuteronomy 17:14
precepts.why:
“the most High ruleth in the kingdom of men, and giveth it to whomsoever he will, and setteth up over it the basest of men.” It does not matter who you vote for; he puts whoever he wants. Donald Trump is one of the basest of men, a caricature and TV personality from The Apprentice, just as Ronald Reagan was an actor. His orange skin is telling you what he is about: he is Esau, the red man. The Most High puts these men over us so we can see: you wanted the other nations to rule over you besides me, and this is what happens.

Deuteronomy 17:14 shows that desire in our people: “When thou art come unto the land which the Lord thy God giveth thee, and shalt possess it, and shalt dwell therein, and shalt say, I will set a king over me, like as all the nations that are about me”. We are not satisfied with the King of kings and Lord of lords, Christ, being over us. We always want to be like the other nations. That is why we dye our hair blonde, put in the contacts, put on the suit and tie, go to their universities and get their education, and assimilate to their way of life.

But the law says “Thou shalt in any wise set him king over thee, whom the Lord thy God shall choose: one from among thy brethren shalt thou set king over thee: thou mayest not set a stranger over thee, which is not thy brother.” We have to have a king of our own people, who is for our people, not a base man out for the interest of corporations that rob and steal our resources. We are not supposed to vote for other nations to be over us. Thus saith the Lord.

The same goes for our people in Latin America. In Mexico and in Argentina, where an Italian was set up, what are they doing for you? Nothing, not a damn thing. You cannot set up people of other nations over you. That is why the Most High sets the basest of men over Israel: to show us what it means to choose a stranger over the king he chose.

precepts.label: Hebrews 1:9
precepts.why:
Christ told Peter to forgive seventy times seven, and Christ never put numbers out just to put them there. Seven represents completion, but what is seventy times seven? Daniel shows it: “Seventy weeks are determined upon thy people and upon thy holy city”. That is 490 years, from Persia to Christ, “to finish the transgression, and to make an end of sins, and to make reconciliation for iniquity, and to bring in everlasting righteousness, and to seal up the vision and prophecy, and to anoint the most Holy.”

Who is the most Holy that is anointed? Hebrews 1:9 explains it: “Thou hast loved righteousness, and hated iniquity; therefore God, even thy God, hath anointed thee with the oil of gladness above thy fellows.” That is talking about Christ. Where Daniel says “to anoint the most Holy”, that is Christ.

So the seventy weeks run “unto the Messiah the Prince”, which is Jesus Christ, and the reconciliation for iniquity and the end of sins come through him. The prophecy was 490 years, completing that perfection through Christ, because we needed that mercy. We couldn't sacrifice when we were enslaved under Babylon and Persia; we were always in captivity, going from one captivity to the next, so we needed Christ.

The apostles said it: “Him hath God exalted with his right hand to be a Prince and a Saviour, for to give repentance to Israel”. That is why he told Peter to forgive his brother seventy times seven: because he forgave us seventy times seven. He is that complete perfection. But don't take him for granted.

precepts.label: Luke 21:20
precepts.why:
“And after threescore and two weeks shall Messiah be cut off, but not for himself”: cut off for the children of Israel. “and the people of the prince that shall come shall destroy the city and the sanctuary”. That prince that shall come and destroy the sanctuary is Titus. “and the end thereof shall be with a flood, and unto the end of the war desolations are determined.” The flood is 70 AD, the destruction, and us being led away into captivity.

Christ spoke of that same desolation: “And when ye shall see Jerusalem compassed with armies, then know that the desolation thereof is nigh.” What armies? The Roman armies. That is what Daniel 9:26 is speaking of, the prince that shall come and destroy the city and the sanctuary.

Then Daniel 9:27: “in the midst of the week he shall cause the sacrifice and the oblation to cease”: the temple being destroyed. “and for the overspreading of abominations he shall make it desolate, even until the consummation”. The Roman armies around Jerusalem were the sign that the desolation determined in the seventy weeks was at hand.

So the 490 years end with Christ cut off for us and the desolation of the city by Titus. After that there was no sacrifice for us but Christ, and that is why his sacrifice is our only way through to perfection.

precepts.label: Micah 2:10
precepts.why:
“in their affliction they will seek me early.” Why do we have to get deported? So that we seek God early. A lot of our people think this is the American dream, this is what life is about: get a house, get a car, barbecue on the weekend, watch sports, send your kids to college. No, that is Esau's way of life. This is death, this is oppression, and the Most High has to afflict us to remind us that this is not our rest.

Micah says it: “Arise ye, and depart”. Separate yourself from these heathen nations, these strangers, the real aliens. “for this is not your rest”. You were not brought here on slave ships to be comfortable, to assimilate, or to be friends with these heathen nations. You see the betrayal time and time again when you make a league with the strangers. “Our necks are under persecution: we labour, and have no rest”: we work and we have to watch our backs for ICE agents who come to our places of business and our homes, arrest us and kidnap our children.

“because it is polluted”: wicked, evil, deceptive. Witchcraft is in this place, so bad that it has you bleaching your skin, blonding your hair, putting in contacts, starving yourself. “it shall destroy you”: it destroyed Sammy Sosa, Serena Williams, Lil' Kim. Those are the celebrities Esau upholds so our people look up to them and want to be like them. It is witchcraft to make a black man hate himself so much that he destroys his own face.

“even with a sore destruction.” Destruction is coming to this place; this kingdom is not going to last forever. We are in the last days, so we have to get our minds right and our spirits right. There is much work to be done, especially for you so-called Latinos: Judah has shown us the way, and now it is our turn. When you see a head of state like Nicolás Maduro kidnapped and his country's resources stolen, that is for you to wake up. Seek his face, and see in the scriptures that he looks just like us.

precepts.label: Obadiah 1:3
precepts.why:
The vision of Obadiah is a prophecy concerning Edom, a time to come, and we must be occupied in prophecies. The Lord says, “Behold, I have made thee small among the heathen: thou art greatly despised.” Edom will be greatly despised. Then he shows why: “The pride of thine heart hath deceived thee”. They are so prideful that they themselves are deceived.

“Thou that dwellest in the clefts of the rock”: they are the cavemen. So Karen has nerve telling you don't park there, you don't belong here, being black while in Starbucks. You was in a cave. Now their pride has deceived them into thinking they are the wise of the earth, the most civilized of the earth. No: they are the most demonic of the earth.

“Whose habitation is high; that saith in his heart, Who shall bring me down to the ground?” They ask that question as though they are God. Ezekiel shows the same prince of Tyrus, for Edom was also called Tyrus: “thou hast said, I am a God, I sit in the seat of God, in the midst of the seas; yet thou art a man, and not God”. Their bases sit in the midst of the seas. “Behold, thou art wiser than Daniel; there is no secret that they can hide from thee”: through all their technological advances they listen through your smart TV and your phone, and by that wisdom and traffic they got riches and lifted up their heart.

That pride grows from the weaponry given to that line from Tubal-cain and Lamech down to Esau, who by his sword would live. The Lord created the smith and the waster. In Isaiah the same one is called Lucifer and the king of Babylon, who weakened the nations through war: “I will ascend above the heights of the clouds; I will be like the most High.” With all this military might they feel like they are the Most High, and people see it and say he must be God or God must be with them.

But the answer to “Who shall bring me down to the ground?” is the Lord. “How art thou fallen from heaven, O Lucifer”. He is going to fall because his pride has reached up unto heaven, and when these devils fall, the whole earth will finally be at rest.

thread.text: Hear now, O Joshua the high priest, thou, and thy fellows that sit before thee: for they are men wondered at: for, behold, I will bring forth my servant the BRANCH.

classes.title: The Nativity: the Bloodline, Birthright, & the Messiah

precepts.label: Zechariah 4:7
precepts.why:
“for, behold, I will bring forth my servant the BRANCH.” Who is that? Christ. And the next chapter says who brings him forth: “Who art thou, O great mountain? before Zerubbabel thou shalt become a plain.” The great mountain is Babylon, made a plain, destroyed.

“and he shall bring forth the headstone thereof with shoutings, crying, Grace, grace unto it.” Who shall bring forth the headstone? Zerubbabel. Chapter 3 said the Lord will bring forth his servant the Branch; here Zerubbabel brings forth the headstone, which is the same as the Branch. And the headstone brings grace unto us.

How will Zerubbabel bring him forth? Through his line. And Zerubbabel comes out of Solomon's line. Matthew 1 shows it: “And after they were brought to Babylon, Jechonias begat Salathiel; and Salathiel begat Zorobabel”, born in Babylon, and from Zorobabel down to “Jacob begat Joseph the husband of Mary, of whom was born Jesus, who is called Christ.” Joseph comes out of the line of kings, the kingdom of Solomon, heir to the throne, but in captivity, with Rome calling the shots and an Edomite, Herod, on the throne, until Christ returns and conquers Edom. There is no scripture that says Jeconiah's line was cursed from being kings; that doctrine was made to justify a virgin birth. The Zerubbabel of Luke 3 is a different one, of Nathan's line: Joseph is written there because he inherited Heli's inheritance as his son-in-law, Heli being Mary's father with no sons.

precepts.label: Psalms 118:22
precepts.why:
Zechariah says, “For behold the stone that I have laid before Joshua; upon one stone shall be seven eyes.” The Branch and the stone are Christ. Then Zerubbabel “shall bring forth the headstone thereof.”

What is the headstone? “The stone which the builders refused is become the head stone of the corner.” Who is the Branch, who is the stone? It's the same thing. The headstone Zerubbabel brings forth is the same stone laid before Joshua, and the same servant the Branch the Lord said he would bring forth: Christ, refused by the builders and made the head of the corner.

So when the Lord says “I will remove the iniquity of that land in one day”, he is going into Christ. The stone laid before Joshua the high priest and his fellows, men wondered at for a sign, is the Christ who would come through Zerubbabel's loins.

precepts.label: Ephesians 2:20
precepts.why:
Zerubbabel built the second temple, so he brought forth a literal stone with a foundation. That's the first level. But it is twofold: he also brought forth the other stone through his loins, to build up the temple which is us here in the room.

“And are built upon the foundation of the apostles and prophets, Jesus Christ himself being the chief corner stone”: the chief corner stone, the headstone. “In whom all the building fitly framed together groweth unto an holy temple in the Lord”: that's us. “In whom ye also are builded together for an habitation of God through the Spirit.”

So we are that holy temple that Christ builds. Zerubbabel laid the foundation of the second temple, and he brought forth the same stone and the same foundation, which is Christ, on whom we are built. Praise the Lord for that.

Obadiah is spoken “concerning Edom”, the same Esau that God hated in Malachi. “Behold, I have made thee small among the heathen: thou art greatly despised.” God made him low, and he hated it.

“The pride of thine heart hath deceived thee, thou that dwellest in the clefts of the rock, whose habitation is high; that saith in his heart, Who shall bring me down to the ground?” That is the one who dwelt in the cliffs of the rocks, in the mountains: cave dwellers, Caucasians, troglodytes. He was displaced out of his land and ended up in the Caucasus Mountains, and when he gained power on the earth he said in his heart that nobody could bring him down.

“Though thou exalt thyself as the eagle”: Greece, Rome, Spain, Portugal, they all rose up as the eagle, and America rose up as the eagle. “And though thou set thy nest among the stars”: gaining power out in space, space travel. How did he get to the stars? Because Satan gave him power to do it: technology, rockets, rocket science, nuclear bombs.

“Thence will I bring thee down, saith the Lord.” It is the same thing God said in Malachi. Edom said “we will return and build the desolate places”: the Renaissance, the rebirth, building up Europe into a superpower on the earth. “They shall build, but I will throw down”. They will rise up again in power, but the Most High himself will bring them down, and they are “the border of wickedness”, the beginning and the end of all wickedness on the earth, with his people, “against whom the Lord hath indignation for ever.”

precepts.label: Genesis 29:22-23
precepts.why:
Matthew says Mary was espoused to Joseph, and “before they came together, she was found with child of the Holy Ghost.” What does “came together” mean? Genesis 29 shows the custom. Jacob served seven years for Rachel, then said, “Give me my wife, for my days are fulfilled, that I may go in unto her.” “And Laban gathered together all the men of the place, and made a feast. And it came to pass in the evening, that he took Leah his daughter, and brought her to him; and he went in unto her.”

The feast is the coming together. Coming together was the customary wedding feast, the same custom seen with Tobit. So before Joseph and Mary came together in the wedding feast, they lay together. There was no fornication, because they were already espoused. Espousal is marriage: once the father made the promise, she could not go and marry another, and a man who lies with a betrothed woman commits adultery. That is why the angel called Mary Joseph's wife. She was his wife by espousal, not because he had lain with her; sex alone does not make a marriage.

Then “Joseph her husband, being a just man, and not willing to make her a publick example, was minded to put her away privily.” The commentators say that means he meant to divorce her secretly, because the child was not his. But if a just man's espoused wife were pregnant by another man, the law said she must die; a just man would not hide her. Put her away privily means hide her, the way “Elisabeth conceived, and hid herself five months.” A public example means being put to death in public. Had Mary gone back to her father's house showing, they would have said she played the harlot, just as they said of Tamar at three months.

So here is the question: why would a just man hide a pregnant woman he did not impregnate? And if she had committed adultery, why would a just man hide her sin? There is no way around that question. Minded means he was thinking about it: he was going to hide her so nothing would happen to her for what the two of them had done, because the child was his.

thread.label: Matthew 1:20-23

precepts.label: 2 Samuel 7:12
precepts.why:
The Lord promised David a king out of his own body: “And when thy days be fulfilled, and thou shalt sleep with thy fathers, I will set up thy seed after thee, which shall proceed out of thy bowels, and I will establish his kingdom.”

The seed that proceeds out of David's bowels is the promised king. So when the angel came to Joseph in the dream, he called him “Joseph, thou son of David”. The line is Joseph's, David's line.

The angel said, “fear not to take unto thee Mary thy wife: for that which is conceived in her is of the Holy Ghost.” That which is conceived in her is of the prophecy of 2 Samuel: the seed promised to David, coming out of his bowels.

That is why the Nativity begins with the bloodline. The child Mary conceived is the fulfilling of the promise made to David, that God would set up his seed after him and establish his kingdom.

precepts.label: Psalms 132:11
precepts.why:
The promise to David was sworn: “The Lord hath sworn in truth unto David; he will not turn from it; Of the fruit of thy body will I set upon thy throne.”

The Lord swore it in truth, and he will not turn from it. The king on David's throne would be the fruit of David's body. That is the same promise as 2 Samuel 7:12, the seed that shall proceed out of David's bowels.

So when the angel said to Joseph, “Joseph, thou son of David, fear not to take unto thee Mary thy wife: for that which is conceived in her is of the Holy Ghost”, that which is conceived in her is of the prophecy: the fruit of David's body that the Lord swore to set upon his throne. The line runs through Joseph, the son of David.

“And she shall bring forth a son, and thou shalt call his name JESUS: for he shall save his people from their sins.” The son is the fruit of David's body, sworn in truth, set on David's throne.

precepts.label: Acts 2:30
precepts.why:
Peter said of David: “Therefore being a prophet, and knowing that God had sworn with an oath to him, that of the fruit of his loins, according to the flesh, he would raise up Christ to sit on his throne”.

God swore to David that of the fruit of his loins he would raise up Christ, and notice the words: according to the flesh. Not according to the spirit. Christ sits on David's throne as the fruit of David's loins in the flesh.

That is why the angel spoke to “Joseph, thou son of David”, and why “that which is conceived in her is of the Holy Ghost” means it is of the prophecy: the promise sworn to David in 2 Samuel 7 and Psalm 132 that the king would come out of his bowels, the fruit of his body.

So the child of Matthew 1 is the Christ God swore to raise up of the fruit of David's loins, according to the flesh, to sit on his throne. The bloodline is the birthright.

precepts.label: Romans 1:3
precepts.why:
Paul says it plainly: “Concerning his Son Jesus Christ our Lord, which was made of the seed of David according to the flesh”. According to what? The flesh.

According to the flesh, he was made like you and I: made flesh and blood like unto his brethren, like his children. The same thing.

That is how Matthew 1 reads. Joseph was minded to put Mary away privily, “But while he thought on these things”, not did them but only thought about doing them, the angel appeared to him saying, “Joseph, thou son of David, fear not to take unto thee Mary thy wife: for that which is conceived in her is of the Holy Ghost.” That which is conceived in her is of the prophecy: the seed promised to David in 2 Samuel 7 and Psalm 132, of the fruit of his loins according to the flesh.

So Jesus Christ our Lord was made of the seed of David according to the flesh. He came into this world as a son of man, made flesh and blood like his brethren, and that is how he fulfils the promise to David.

thread.label: Matthew 1:21
thread.text: And she shall bring forth a son, and thou shalt call his name JESUS: for he shall save his people from their sins.

classes.title: 70 Times 7: The Perfection of Mercy Through Christ

precepts.label: John 1:29
precepts.why:
We did not return to what the Most High commanded, the feasts he told us to go back to, and that is why we were in need of a saviour, an ultimate sacrifice. From Abraham to David, from David to the carrying away into Babylon, and from Babylon to Christ were fourteen generations each; we were always in slavery.

“And she shall bring forth a son, and thou shalt call his name JESUS: for he shall save his people from their sins.” His name means he saves. His people: the Israelites only. From their sins. That is why he was the ultimate sacrifice.

His cousin John expounds on it: “Behold the Lamb of God, which taketh away the sin of the world.” The Lamb of God. Christ was that perfect, ultimate sacrifice, the lamb that takes away the sins of the people he came to save.

precepts.label: Hebrews 10:5-8
precepts.why:
To expound further on Christ being the ultimate sacrifice: “Wherefore when he cometh into the world, he saith, Sacrifice and offering thou wouldest not, but a body hast thou prepared me”. The Pharisees watched Christ in the synagogue so they might accuse him, and Luke shows how far they went: “the scribes and the Pharisees began to urge him vehemently, and to provoke him to speak of many things.” They were trying to get him to come out of the spirit, to speak vehemently and say things he should not say.

But no, Christ kept it spiritual, according to the Bible, the way we should.

“Laying wait for him, and seeking to catch something out of his mouth, that they might accuse him.” Trying to catch him and have him slip up in his speech. The same Pharisees back then are here today in 2026, provoking and laying wait for something to catch out of our mouths, and the answer is the same: stay in the spirit.

precepts.label: Luke 20:20
precepts.why:
They did not only watch Christ from the outside. “And they watched him, and sent forth spies, which should feign themselves just men, that they might take hold of his words, that so they might deliver him unto the power and authority of the governor.”

Spies pretending to be just men, sitting among his hearers, waiting to take hold of his words and hand him over to the governor.

Oh, we might have a few of them up in here. We might have a few of them up in our Atlanta congregation, New York congregation, Mississippi congregation. We know you're there, biding your time. The Pharisees watched Christ on the sabbath that they might accuse him, and they still send forth spies today, feigning themselves just men.

precepts.label: Ruth 4:13
precepts.why:
Gabriel tells Mary, “thou shalt conceive in thy womb, and bring forth a son”. It is the same word used of her cousin: “And after those days his wife Elisabeth conceived”. What does it mean to conceive? To conceive you need seed; the man’s seed has to go in and fertilize the egg. Some might be confused, so Ruth shows how that happens.

“So Boaz took Ruth, and she was his wife: and when he went in unto her, the Lord gave her conception, and she bare a son.” When Boaz went in unto her, the Lord gave her conception. That is how it works: a husband goes in unto his wife, and the Lord gives the conception.

And when Luke 1:28 says the angel “came in unto her”, he came in and talked with her. He did not come in and have sex with her; he came in and talked to her, plain and simple. So when Luke 1:31 says Mary shall conceive, it is conception the way Ruth conceived, the Lord giving it when her husband came unto her. It could well have been the first time Joseph touched her that the Lord made her conceive.

precepts.label: Leviticus 12:2
precepts.why:
The law shows what conceiving is: “Speak unto the children of Israel, saying, If a woman have conceived seed, and born a man child: then she shall be unclean seven days”. She conceived what? Seed.

A woman conceives seed through intercourse. That is the same seed Onan spilled on the ground in Genesis 38, knowing the inheritance would not be his. It is the same exact thing.

So Luke 1:31, “thou shalt conceive in thy womb, and bring forth a son”, is a woman conceiving seed and bearing a man child. It is said to Mary in the same form of words as to Zacharias about Elisabeth: “thy wife Elisabeth shall bear thee a son, and thou shalt call his name John,” and “shalt call his name JESUS.” The same thing being done, the same thing being said.

precepts.label: Wisdom of Solomon 19:7-8
precepts.why:
Luke 1:35 says “the power of the Highest shall overshadow thee”. What does overshadow mean? Wisdom of Solomon shows it: “For the whole creature in his proper kind was fashioned again anew, serving the peculiar commandments that were given unto them, that thy children might be kept without hurt”. The whole creature is Israel, the whole nation that came out of Egypt, made new, serving the peculiar commandments.

“As namely, a cloud shadowing the camp; and where water stood before, dry land appeared; and out of the Red sea a way without impediment; and out of the violent stream a green field: Wherethrough all the people went that were defended with thy hand, seeing thy marvellous strange wonders.”

What did the cloud shadowing the camp do for us at the Red Sea? It led us. It guided us through the Red Sea, and the people went through “defended with thy hand.” That is what overshadow means: to lead, guide and defend.

So when the angel says the power of the Highest shall overshadow Mary, it is not the spirit coming into her and making her pregnant. It is the Lord guiding and defending her, leading her to where she had to go.

precepts.label: Baruch 5:7-9
precepts.why:
Baruch gives another one. Overshadow does not mean that it got her impregnated. It means to guide her to where she had to go. “For God hath appointed that every high hill, and banks of long continuance, should be cast down, and valleys filled up, to make even the ground, that Israel may go safely in the glory of God”.

“Moreover even the woods and every sweetsmelling tree shall overshadow Israel by the commandment of God. For God shall lead Israel with joy in the light of his glory”. The trees shall overshadow Israel, for God shall lead Israel. To overshadow is to lead, guide or defend.

So in Luke 1:35 the Lord would lead Mary to Joseph. When it says overshadow thee, it means he will guide and lead her, like he led Zacharias home to his wife to lay with her. That is what it is talking about, not him overshadowing her into pregnancy.

precepts.label: Proverbs 20:24
precepts.why:
This goes with overshadow: the Lord guided Mary, and she went and came together with her husband. “Man’s goings are of the Lord; how can a man then understand his own way?”

A man’s goings are of the Lord because the Lord guides us and overshadows us in everyday life. Sometimes you are walking in the street, something tells you to pick something up off the ground, and a car goes right by where you would have been. Why? The Lord was there guiding you.

“how can a man then understand his own way?” Remember, Mary did not understand. She said, “How shall this be, seeing I know not a man?” She was espoused to Joseph but had not yet come together with him. The Lord said, don’t worry, you are going to fulfil the scriptures; I am going to guide you. She could not understand her way, but the Most High had plans for her, and he guided her, the same way he guided every one of us here.

precepts.label: John 17:11,20-22
precepts.why:
The priest explaining the sign of the cross as three distinct persons of one essence never opens a Bible. The one scripture he leans on is John 10:30: “I and my Father are one.” That's all he has. But Christ says it again in John 17, and there he tells you what one means.

“And now I am no more in the world, but these are in the world, and I come to thee. Holy Father, keep through thine own name those whom thou hast given me, that they may be one, as we are.” These are his disciples. If one means one being, one essence, then Christ and the disciples are all one being too. That's not what it's talking about. They are one because they speak the same things, say the same things, in the same spirit.

“Neither pray I for these alone, but for them also which shall believe on me through their word; That they all may be one; as thou, Father, art in me, and I in thee, that they also may be one in us”. “And the glory which thou gavest me I have given them; that they may be one, even as we are one”. So are they all one entity? Do they form Voltron, do the fusion dance, become a Megazord? It's madness; it's ridiculous. One means one in spirit and speech, not one entity.

That is why they never bring out the Bible. The trinity was argued out over centuries of councils, borrowed from Greek philosophy, confusion upon confusion, and God is not the author of confusion. The Bible is plain: “to us there is but one God, the Father, of whom are all things, and we in him; and one Lord Jesus Christ, by whom are all things, and we by him.” Paul warned, “Beware lest any man spoil you through philosophy and vain deceit”.

precepts.label: Matthew 24:9
precepts.why:
The rulers “commanded them not to speak at all nor teach in the name of Jesus”, and again: “Did not we straitly command you that ye should not teach in this name?” We read that and say it could never happen in America. Don't fool yourself. It will happen here.

Christ warned it: “Then shall they deliver you up to be afflicted, and shall kill you: and ye shall be hated of all nations for my name’s sake.” Imagine they shut your bank account down. Now you can't pay your rent, your mortgage, your car note; you lose your car, your home, and maybe your wife: that's what you get for teaching that Bible, don't block Jesus. Everybody says, I'm strong, I can go through it. Wait till that day, with a newborn baby and you can't get infant formula. Some will say, I'm going back to being a Christian so I can get access to my money.

That hatred starts with the followers of Christ, but it applies to all twelve tribes of Israel. Look at the news: black and brown people killed, and they cry, what did we do to these white people? Why did they kill Sandra Bland? Why did they kill Tamir Rice? Christ said you would be hated of all nations. Christ is our king whether you accept it or not, and the white man looks at you and says, these are the people of Christ. You are the children of God, and they are the children of the devil. You might not like it, but it's true.

precepts.label: 2 Esdras 7:14
precepts.why:
Being hated of all nations is not only for those who teach the Bible; Ezra shows who it will affect. “For the entrances of the elder world were wide and sure, and brought immortal fruit.” The elder world was paradise in the time of Adam. “If then they that live labour not to enter these strait and vain things, they can never receive those that are laid up for them.”

You have to enter those hard things to enter paradise. The angel is telling Ezra that if we don't go through the hardships of Jacob's trouble, we can never get paradise. If you decide to kill yourself before it happens, you cannot get paradise. If you say, I'm going to join another religion to escape punishment from these other nations, you will never receive it.

Read on: “Nevertheless the righteous shall suffer strait things, and hope for wide”. The righteous shall suffer hard things, that is Jacob's trouble, and hope for paradise. “for they that have done wickedly have suffered the strait things, and yet shall not see the wide.” The wicked Israelites are going through Jacob's trouble too, but they are not going to see the kingdom.

So when Christ said you shall be hated of all nations, it covers all Israel. Whether you teach or not, the strait things are coming; the only question is whether you come out of them into what is laid up for you. That is why you cannot run from the persecution when they command us not to teach in his name.

precepts.label: Ecclesiastes 1:9
precepts.why:
“And at that time there was a great persecution against the church which was at Jerusalem; and they were all scattered abroad”. We saw persecution against our brothers in France; it hasn't gotten here yet, and they say America is the major hub. When it happens, can you stand the rain? That's why we say don't take the convocations lightly.

People read these things and say, oh, that's old time. But Solomon says: “The thing that hath been, it is that which shall be; and that which is done is that which shall be done: and there is no new thing under the sun.” That's you and me. We read Maccabees and Acts 8:1 and say that could never happen again? You're simple as hell. What happened in 1 Maccabees 1 and Daniel 3 is what Revelation 13 speaks of, no buying and selling, and it leads to death.

Paul said the same thing: “For whatsoever things were written aforetime were written for our learning, that we through patience and comfort of the scriptures might have hope.” Those old-time things were written for us to learn from, because they are going to happen again. We need patience and the comfort of the scriptures because we are going to go through what our ancestors went through: how did they deal with it, how did they survive?

Herod killed James and, because it pleased them, took Peter also. And Trump joked about bringing back public executions. The Christians don't understand what is about to come; in here we understand, because what has been is what shall be.

precepts.label: James 1:21-25
precepts.why:
In Galatians Paul says you are not justified by the works of the law, and Christians say, see, we don’t have to keep the commandments; Christ died for us, just believe. Then the same Paul writes, “For not the hearers of the law are just before God, but the doers of the law shall be justified.” Was Paul schizophrenic? No. The law in Galatians is animal sacrifice, explained in Hebrews 7, 9 and 10, which Christ did away with. The law here is the commandments. Faith comes first, and then the works follow.

Christ’s brother James answers the same way: “Wherefore lay apart all filthiness and superfluity of naughtiness”: lay aside all sin. “And receive with meekness the engrafted word, which is able to save your souls.” The engrafted word is the law and the testimony. Some heard in church that the law cannot save you, only Christ can. The law in Christ saves you; keeping God’s commandments can save your soul.

“But be ye doers of the word, and not hearers only, deceiving your own selves.” That takes you right back to Romans 2:13. Christianity tells you that you do not have to keep God’s commandments and will still be saved; they deceive themselves and others. “For if any be a hearer of the word, and not a doer, he is like unto a man beholding his natural face in a glass: For he beholdeth himself, and goeth his way, and straightway forgetteth what manner of man he was.” He reads the Bible, says yeah okay, and goes back to sinning, looking in the mirror and forgetting what he saw.

“But whoso looketh into the perfect law of liberty, and continueth therein, he being not a forgetful hearer, but a doer of the work, this man shall be blessed in his deed.” The work is the commandments; blessed in his deed is justified. Christ gave us liberty from the law of sin and death, the sacrifices under which a man “died without mercy”, but that liberty is not freedom from doing the commandments. The doers of the law shall be justified.

precepts.label: Isaiah 8:20
precepts.why:
James says, “receive with meekness the engrafted word, which is able to save your souls.” What is the engrafted word? Isaiah answers it: “To the law and to the testimony: if they speak not according to this word, it is because there is no light in them.”

The law and the testimony is the word. So the word James says is able to save your soul, the word we must be doers of and not hearers only, is the law and the testimony: the commandments of God.

That is why Paul could say, “not the hearers of the law are just before God, but the doers of the law shall be justified.” The law he means there is the commandments, the engrafted word, not the sacrifices that Christ did away with.

So when the church says the law cannot save you, they are not speaking according to this word. Those who speak not according to the law and the testimony have no light in them. The word saves, Christ saves, and the doer of the word is the one justified.

precepts.label: Lamentations 2:13
precepts.why:
Paul proves from the Psalms that Israel became filthy: “They are all gone aside, they are all together become filthy: there is none that doeth good, no, not one.” The whole nation was broken. Jeremiah laments that same breaking: “What thing shall I liken to thee, O daughter of Jerusalem? what shall I equal to thee, that I may comfort thee, O virgin daughter of Zion? for thy breach is great like the sea: who can heal thee?”

A breach is a split or a tear. Our breach is great like the sea. Who can heal us? Christ, our saviour.

Isaiah shows the healing: “And the Lord shall guide thee continually, and satisfy thy soul in drought, and make fat thy bones: and thou shalt be like a watered garden, and like a spring of water, whose waters fail not.” When our souls are in drought, the Lord is going to water us and heal us. “And they that shall be of thee shall build the old waste places”, the waste places we made when we became filthy. “Thou shalt raise up the foundations of many generations; and thou shalt be called, The repairer of the breach, The restorer of paths to dwell in.”

The root word of reparations is repair. The repairer of the breach: that is the reparations right there. Both Jews and Gentiles, Judah and Ephraim, were “all under sin” and torn apart, and the one who heals that breach is Christ, repairing and restoring Israel.

precepts.label: Acts 15:14-17
precepts.why:
Paul says “we have before proved both Jews and Gentiles, that they are all under sin”, and the Gentiles there are Israelites. Acts 15 shows the same Gentiles being restored: “Simeon hath declared how God at the first did visit the Gentiles, to take out of them a people for his name.” That references what took place in Acts 10, and we understand that is talking about Israel.

“And to this agree the words of the prophets; as it is written, After this I will return, and will build again the tabernacle of David, which is fallen down; and I will build again the ruins thereof, and I will set it up”. Build again: that is the reconciliation, that is the reparation. It had fallen down because we became filthy, and God restores the waste places. Who is that? All twelve tribes of Israel.

Then verse 17: “That the residue of men might seek after the Lord”. The residue is the rest of the nations outside of the twelve tribes: Edom and the others. “And all the Gentiles, upon whom my name is called”: that is the Christians, and the Jews.

They try to include themselves in our reconciliation, our restoration and our adoption. But the building again is of David’s tabernacle, the twelve tribes; the residue only seeks after the Lord once Israel is set up again.

precepts.label: Amos 9:11-12
precepts.why:
Acts 15 quotes the prophet Amos: “In that day will I raise up the tabernacle of David that is fallen, and close up the breaches thereof”. The breaches are the tear, the split, like the breach “great like the sea” in Lamentations. Remember, the root word of reparations is to repair.

“And I will raise up his ruins, and I will build it as in the days of old”. This is the restoring of Israel, both kingdoms that Paul proved “are all under sin” in Romans 3, repaired and raised up as in the days of old.

Then: “That they may possess the remnant of Edom, and of all the heathen, which are called by my name, saith the Lord that doeth this.” That they, all twelve tribes, may possess the remnant of Edom and of the heathen called by his name.

So you see, other nations cannot be involved in our reconciliation, our restoration or our reparation. The ones called by his name, the Christians and the Jews, are not the tabernacle being raised; they are what Israel possesses once it is raised. This goes back to the classes before on Romans 11 and Acts 10.

precepts.label: Nehemiah 10:33
precepts.why:
Romans 4:2 says “For if Abraham were justified by works, he hath whereof to glory; but not before God.” What works is Paul talking about? Nehemiah condenses them into one verse: “For the shewbread, and for the continual meat offering, and for the continual burnt offering, of the sabbaths, of the new moons, for the set feasts, and for the holy things, and for the sin offerings to make an atonement for Israel, and for all the work of the house of our God.”

Continual means it was done all the time, daily, annually. And “to make an atonement” goes back to the word justify: atone, justify and reconcile are the same thing. So the works Paul is talking about are temple sacrifice, temple law. When Paul wrote, the temple was still standing and the Jews in Rome were still going to it and still sacrificing, and they believed their works were enough.

Abraham shows the order. In Genesis 15 the Lord promised the old man an heir out of his own bowels and seed as the stars, “And he believed in the Lord; and he counted it to him for righteousness.” He was promised the land and he believed. Only then was he told to take the heifer, the goat, the ram and the birds and divide them. Faith came first, then the works.

When brothers don't study Paul's letters, they start saying Paul's letters are not authoritative, and speak evil of dignities, of Paul, Mark and Luke, because they weren't of the twelve. When you speak evil of dignities, your mind is blinded and you end up teaching a whole different gospel: that the nations can be saved. House negroes are the worst kind of negro. But this is the college course of this school. Know what the works are from Nehemiah, and nobody can come to your school or camp and confound you at Romans 4.

precepts.label: Hebrews 10:28
precepts.why:
Romans 4:4 says “Now to him that worketh is the reward not reckoned of grace, but of debt.” To him that offers sacrifices, the reward is not reckoned of grace or mercy, but of debt, because under Moses there was no grace. Hebrews shows it: “He that despised Moses’ law died without mercy under two or three witnesses”. Without mercy means without grace.

If you chose to do something worthy of death that an animal could not atone for, you had to die. If you broke the Sabbath, you couldn't atone with an animal. Homosexuality, you couldn't atone with an animal. Idolatry, you couldn't atone with an animal. And if you chose not to sacrifice at all, you had to die. So you were indebted to offer continual sacrifices all the time: continual burnt offerings, drink offerings, sin offerings.

The prophets said the temple would be destroyed. Once the temple is gone, where are your works? If your salvation rests on sacrificing an animal and there is no animal, no priest and no temple to atone with, by default you have condemned yourself. That is why faith in Christ has to supersede the works.

“But to him that worketh not”, him that does not offer sacrifice, “but believeth on him that justifieth the ungodly, his faith is counted for righteousness.” Christ justifies the ungodly through his death. Just as with Abraham, who was counted faithful before he sacrificed animals, God “imputeth righteousness without works”. Israel could keep sacrificing while the temple stood, but Christ had to come first in their minds, or they were in debt.
