classes.title: 70 Times 7: The Perfection of Mercy Through Christ

precepts.label: 2 Esdras 8:52
precepts.why:
“For we which have believed do enter into rest.” What is that rest that is promised? Ezra shows it: “For unto you is paradise opened, the tree of life is planted, the time to come is prepared, plenteousness is made ready, a city is builded, and rest is allowed, yea, perfect goodness and wisdom.”

This paradise is spoken to the Israelites. It is not talking about all nations. Paradise opened, the tree of life planted, a city builded and rest allowed: that is what is left to us, the promise “of entering into his rest.”

“For unto us was the gospel preached, as well as unto them.” The gospel did not begin in the book of Matthew; Christ was taught to our forefathers too. But “the word preached did not profit them, not being mixed with faith in them that heard it.” They disobeyed Christ and were moved with unbelief, and their unbelief is what kept them from entering in. “Let us therefore fear”, then, lest any of us come short of the paradise and the rest that is allowed to Israel.

precepts.label: 2 Esdras 3:5-6
precepts.why:
Paul says God’s works “were finished from the foundation of the world.” The rest is not something new; it was prepared before anything else was. Ezra shows it: “And gavest a body unto Adam without soul, which was the workmanship of thine hands, and didst breathe into him the breath of life, and he was made living before thee. And thou leadest him into paradise, which thy right hand had planted, before ever the earth came forward.”

Paradise was here before the earth came forth. Before Christ said the evening and the morning were the first day, paradise was already here. That is the paradise opened to Israel in 2 Esdras 8:52, where the tree of life is planted and rest is allowed.

So when Hebrews says the works were finished from the foundation of the world, it is telling you the rest was already created and waiting. Then “he spake in a certain place of the seventh day on this wise, And God did rest the seventh day from all his works.” That number seven keeps coming back: the seventh day Sabbath points to that rest God prepared from the beginning.

precepts.label: Micah 4:10
precepts.why:
“For he that is entered into his rest, he also hath ceased from his own works, as God did from his.” Paul is making a comparison between our works and God’s. God worked, then rested; so must we. Micah shows the labour: “Be in pain, and labour to bring forth, O daughter of Zion, like a woman in travail: for now shalt thou go forth out of the city.”

No matter what we are going through, brothers and sisters, we have to be in pain and do this work. Be in pain to bring forth the kingdom of heaven on earth.

That is why Paul says “Let us labour therefore to enter into that rest, lest any man fall after the same example of unbelief.” Labour, labour in pain, bring forth your works to enter into that rest, which is the kingdom. Rest is entered by labour. The generation in the wilderness fell because of unbelief; the daughter of Zion must travail to bring forth.

precepts.label: Revelation 14:13
precepts.why:
“For he that is entered into his rest, he also hath ceased from his own works, as God did from his.” Revelation shows who rests and why: “Blessed are the dead which die in the Lord from henceforth: Yea, saith the Spirit, that they may rest from their labours; and their works do follow them.”

They rest from their labours, and their works follow them. Your works are what are going to allow you to enter in through those gates. The rest is not handed to the idle; it comes after the labour, and the labour goes with you into it.

So “Let us labour therefore to enter into that rest, lest any man fall after the same example of unbelief” that we read of in the wilderness. Labour in pain, bring forth your works, like the daughter of Zion in travail, and then rest from those labours in the kingdom.

precepts.label: Isaiah 14:1-3
precepts.why:
The seventh day Sabbath, resting from our servile work, is a similitude the Most High uses for us resting in the kingdom when it is established. That is the true rest, when we will really rest from servile work. Because after the Sabbath some of us have to go to work on Sunday, then Monday, Tuesday, Wednesday, slaving for Esau.

Isaiah shows the day of that rest: “For the Lord will have mercy on Jacob, and will yet choose Israel, and set them in their own land: and the strangers shall be joined with them, and they shall cleave to the house of Jacob.” The nations are going to be joined with us, but how? “And the people shall take them, and bring them to their place: and the house of Israel shall possess them in the land of the Lord for servants and handmaids: and they shall take them captives, whose captives they were; and they shall rule over their oppressors.” They are our possession.

“And it shall come to pass in the day that the Lord shall give thee rest from thy sorrow, and from thy fear, and from the hard bondage wherein thou wast made to serve.” That is the true rest: rest from our sorrow, from our fear, and from the hard bondage we were made to serve.

That is why “if Jesus had given them rest, then would he not afterward have spoken of another day.” That Jesus is Joshua. Joshua was mighty and smote the Hamites, but we did not get true rest in the land; there were enemies on all sides, the Amalekites and the Hamites we were fighting. The true rest is the kingdom of God on earth, rulership over our enemies. “There remaineth therefore a rest to the people of God.”

precepts.label: 2 Peter 3:7-8
precepts.why:
“And God did rest the seventh day from all his works.” Peter shows how that seventh day reaches forward to the kingdom: “But the heavens and the earth, which are now, by the same word are kept in store, reserved unto fire against the day of judgment and perdition of ungodly men. But, beloved, be not ignorant of this one thing, that one day is with the Lord as a thousand years, and a thousand years as one day.”

One day with the Lord, brothers, is a thousand years. So the seventh day is not only the Sabbath we keep each week; it maps to a thousand years, the reign that comes after the heavens and earth that are now are reserved unto fire against the day of judgment.

That is why “There remaineth therefore a rest to the people of God.” The rest of the seventh day is the similitude, and the thousand years is the substance: the day we reign with Christ, as Revelation 20:4 shows.

precepts.label: Revelation 20:4
precepts.why:
If one day with the Lord is a thousand years, what is the seventh day rest? Revelation shows it: “And I saw thrones, and they sat upon them, and judgment was given unto them: and I saw the souls of them that were beheaded for the witness of Jesus, and for the word of God, and which had not worshipped the beast, neither his image, neither had received his mark upon their foreheads, or in their hands; and they lived and reigned with Christ a thousand years.”

They lived and reigned with Christ a thousand years. That is going into the rest. The seventh day Sabbath represents us resting with Christ, and every seventh day is rehearsing it.

The rest promised in Hebrews is not the land Joshua brought us into, and not only the one day a week before going back to labour in Esau’s system. It is the eternal reign with Christ when he comes back, sitting on thrones with judgment given to us, rulership over our enemies. “There remaineth therefore a rest to the people of God.” Seven represents completion, and the seventh day points to that completion: the kingdom and the thousand years with Christ.

classes.title: Navigating Through Paul's Letters: Works Of The Law & Liberty

precepts.label: Romans 13:8-10
precepts.why:
James 2:8 says “If ye fulfil the royal law according to the scripture, Thou shalt love thy neighbour as thyself, ye do well.” What is the royal law? Romans 13 lays it out.

“Owe no man any thing, but to love one another: for he that loveth another hath fulfilled the law.” What law? Love your neighbour as yourself. “For this, Thou shalt not commit adultery, Thou shalt not kill, Thou shalt not steal, Thou shalt not bear false witness, Thou shalt not covet”: every one of those is the royal law. “And if there be any other commandment”, any other commandment regarding your neighbour outside of those, “it is briefly comprehended in this saying, namely, Thou shalt love thy neighbour as thyself.”

Love your neighbour as yourself is an abbreviation of the six commandments. Of the ten spoken commandments, the first four are how you observe God, and the last six are how you serve your neighbour: honour your father and mother, don’t commit adultery, don’t kill, don’t steal, don’t bear false witness, don’t covet. Those six are briefly comprehended in that one saying. The ten spoken commandments were themselves an abbreviation.

“Love worketh no ill to his neighbour”: no ill like being a respecter of persons, seating the man with the gold ring in a good place and telling the poor man to stand over there. “Therefore love is the fulfilling of the law.” Do we keep it? Yes, you simple Christians. That is the royal law James is talking about, and respect of persons is sin against it.

precepts.label: Matthew 22:34-40
precepts.why:
“But when the Pharisees had heard that he had put the Sadducees to silence, they were gathered together.” Christ had put the Sadducees to shame, and the Pharisees saw how sharp he was. “Then one of them, which was a lawyer, asked him a question, tempting him.”

A lawyer is a scribe. Their job was writing the Bible over and over again, because ink fades and animal skin and paper rip and smear, so it had to be copied again and again. They were the recorders and copyists, and they knew the law and the prophets off top. That is why he was tempting Christ: he already knew the answer. “Master, which is the great commandment in the law?”

“Thou shalt love the Lord thy God with all thy heart, and with all thy soul, and with all thy mind. This is the first and great commandment.” That is the first four of the ten spoken commandments. “And the second is like unto it, Thou shalt love thy neighbour as thyself.” That is the six, the royal law of James 2:8.

“On these two commandments hang all the law and the prophets.” These two are an abbreviation of all the laws. Loving God with all your heart, soul and mind means keeping the Sabbath day holy, the Passover, Tabernacles, Pentecost, the new moons, keeping the congregation, and the dietary law: don’t drink blood, don’t eat pork or shrimp. That is all serving God. The ten are an umbrella over all of them.

precepts.label: Mark 12:28-33
precepts.why:
Mark gives the same account with more detail, and it ties into sacrifice. “And one of the scribes came.” In Matthew he is called a lawyer; in Mark he is called a scribe, because they wrote things over and over and had the law in their minds. There were a bunch of them, but he was bold and spoke up: “Which is the first commandment of all?”

“The first of all the commandments is, Hear, O Israel; The Lord our God is one Lord”: that is Deuteronomy 6:4. “And thou shalt love the Lord thy God with all thy heart, and with all thy soul, and with all thy mind, and with all thy strength: this is the first commandment.” The commandments, the dietary law, the civil law, the sacrificial law, all of that is in there. “And the second is like, namely this, Thou shalt love thy neighbour as thyself. There is none other commandment greater than these.” If you can keep those, you can keep them all.

“Well, Master, thou hast said the truth”: true, true, true. Then verse 33: “to love him with all the heart, and with all the understanding, and with all the soul, and with all the strength, and to love his neighbour as himself, is more than all whole burnt offerings and sacrifices.” It is better than sacrifices. That is why Mark is loved: he makes it clear.

Why is it more than sacrifices? Because Israel would mess around, offer sacrifices, and then hate their neighbour, kill their neighbour, steal from their neighbour, bang their neighbour’s wife or sleep with their neighbour’s husband, but offer the best animal. The Lord said, I don’t care about that stuff. I care about your obedience, loving each other, loving me above the animals.

precepts.label: Sirach 35:1-3
precepts.why:
Mark 12:33 said loving God and your neighbour is more than all whole burnt offerings and sacrifices. Ecclesiasticus 35 says the same.

“He that keepeth the law bringeth offerings enough: he that taketh heed to the commandment offereth a peace offering.” Keeping the law is offering enough.

“He that requiteth a good turn offereth fine flour.” Under the offerings, you offered an animal, or fine flour if you were poor. Here, requiting a good turn, which is loving your neighbour as yourself, is the fine flour. “And he that giveth alms sacrificeth praise.”

“To depart from wickedness is a thing pleasing to the Lord; and to forsake unrighteousness is a propitiation.” Propitiation means mercy, reconciliation. Departing from wickedness toward your neighbour is what reconciles you to God, which is why the royal law of James 2:8 stands above the sacrifices.

precepts.label: 1 Samuel 15:22
precepts.why:
Saul disobeyed a direct order, and through Samuel the Lord asks him a question: “Hath the Lord as great delight in burnt offerings and sacrifices, as in obeying the voice of the Lord?” Answer it.

“Behold, to obey is better than sacrifice, and to hearken than the fat of rams.” The Lord cared about obedience more than animal sacrifices.

That is the same point as Mark 12:33, that loving God and your neighbour “is more than all whole burnt offerings and sacrifices.” Saul wanted to bring the sacrifice after he had disobeyed; Israel wanted to bring the best animal after they had wronged their neighbour. The Lord wants the obedience. And that is why James 2 holds us to the royal law, love thy neighbour as thyself, and not to an offering that covers over a sin against the brother.

precepts.label: Psalms 40:6
precepts.why:
“Sacrifice and offering thou didst not desire; mine ears hast thou opened: burnt offering and sin offering hast thou not required.” This is quoted again in Hebrews 10.

David is saying, you opened my ears, and I understand the spirit: you don’t really care about sacrifices. Remember David wanted to build the temple. But the spirit was revealed to him that the sacrifices were just a placeholder for Christ to show up. He learned that because Christ was speaking through him.

So David realized: you don’t care about sacrifices at all, you care about obedience. That is what Samuel told Saul when he was king, “to obey is better than sacrifice.” And it is why the royal law of James 2, loving the neighbour and not being a respecter of persons, is what God is looking for.

precepts.label: Proverbs 21:3
precepts.why:
“To do justice and judgment is more acceptable to the Lord than sacrifice.”

To do justice and judgment, just like the Lord told Saul to do, is more acceptable than sacrifice. He says it over and over and over again: in Samuel, in the Psalms, in Mark, and here in Proverbs.

Justice and judgment is how you treat your neighbour. In James 2 the assembly seated the rich man in a good place and told the poor man to stand there, and James asks, “Are ye not then partial in yourselves, and are become judges of evil thoughts?” That is the opposite of doing justice and judgment, and no sacrifice would make up for it. Keeping the royal law is what is acceptable to the Lord.

precepts.label: Hosea 6:5-6
precepts.why:
“Therefore have I hewed them by the prophets; I have slain them by the words of my mouth.” The word of God can slay; it is the spirit. “And thy judgments are as the light that goeth forth.”

“For I desired mercy, and not sacrifice; and the knowledge of God more than burnt offerings.” He was not about the sacrifice. That was a schoolmaster, a placeholder. He desired mercy and the knowledge of God.

The Lord eventually said away with it, through the prophets themselves. And that is where James 2:13 lands: “For he shall have judgment without mercy, that hath shewed no mercy; and mercy rejoiceth against judgment.” You shall receive no mercy if you show no mercy. Mercy rejoices against judgment: the Most High chooses to have mercy rather than to judge you for violating the royal law, and he looks for that same mercy in us toward our neighbour.

precepts.label: Judith 16:16
precepts.why:
“For all sacrifice is too little for a sweet savour unto thee, and all the fat is not sufficient for thy burnt offering: but he that feareth the Lord is great at all times.”

All sacrifice is too little. He that fears the Lord is great at all times. The Lord is saying, sacrificing, I don’t care about that; fearing me and obeying me is more important.

That closes the line of scriptures: Mark 12:33, Ecclesiasticus 35, 1 Samuel 15:22, Psalms 40:6, Proverbs 21:3, Hosea 6:6 and Judith 16:16 all say the same thing. Then back to James 2. “For whosoever shall keep the whole law, and yet offend in one point, he is guilty of all.” Christians use this to say that if you sin in one law you break them all, so you can’t keep them at all. But the context is the royal law, love your neighbour as yourself, and James explains it himself: “For he that said, Do not commit adultery, said also, Do not kill.” If you commit no adultery but you kill your brother, you are a transgressor of the royal law.

“So speak ye, and so do, as they that shall be judged by the law of liberty.” Under the old covenant, if you violated the moral law, moved your neighbour’s landmark or slept with your brother’s wife, you got death. Christ redeemed us from that and put us under the law of liberty. So stop doing it.

thread.label: James 2:14-26
thread.text: What doth it profit, my brethren, though a man say he hath faith, and have not works? can faith save him?

classes.title: Navigating Through Paul's Letters: Works Of The Law & Liberty

precepts.label: 2 Esdras 9:7
precepts.why:
“Even so faith, if it hath not works, is dead, being alone.” People say the law can’t save you, you are not justified by the works of the law. Ezra answers it: “And every one that shall be saved, and shall be able to escape by his works, and by faith, whereby ye have believed.”

Everyone that shall be saved shall escape by what? His works. And by faith. Works and faith go hand in hand; you have to have both, as James said. You will be saved by both: not faith alone and no works, not faith and no commandments, not commandments and no faith. That makes no sense; it is dead, being alone.

“though a man say he hath faith, and have not works? can faith save him?” That is like a man saying I got a paycheck, with no job. I get paid tomorrow. You got a job? No. It is the dumbest thing you can say out of your mouth. Your faith proves your works and your works prove your faith. Abraham had faith and kept the commandments of God, and his keeping the commandments proved his faith.

And it goes back to the royal law, loving your neighbour as yourself. Telling a brother with no food and no clothes “be ye warmed and filled”, and giving him nothing, makes no damn sense. Even so, faith without works makes no sense: the faith does not exist.

precepts.label: Revelation 14:12
precepts.why:
“shew me thy faith without thy works, and I will shew thee my faith by my works.” You cannot show faith without works. You show your faith through your actions, which is keeping the commandments of God. John says it in Revelation: “Here is the patience of the saints: here are they that keep the commandments of God, and the faith of Jesus.”

Keep the commandments, and the faith of Jesus. The faith is one, and the commandments are the works. That is what James said, and what Ezra said: saved by works and by faith.

“Thou believest that there is one God; thou doest well: the devils also believe, and tremble.” Even the devils, the unclean spirits, believe in God and are afraid of him. “But wilt thou know, O vain man, that faith without works is dead?” The vain man is the Christianity follower: faith without works, Calvinism, Protestantism, Catholicism. The saints are marked by both, the commandments of God and the faith of Jesus, and one without the other is dead.

precepts.label: Revelation 22:14
precepts.why:
The saints “keep the commandments of God, and the faith of Jesus”, and Revelation shows what the commandments are for: “Blessed are they that do his commandments, that they may have right to the tree of life, and may enter in through the gates into the city.”

That do his commandments: deeds, actions, works. They must do the commandments to enter in through the gates, and have faith in Christ. They go hand in hand.

That is James’ point: “Even so faith, if it hath not works, is dead, being alone.” A man who says he has faith but does no works, who will not keep the commandments, has no right to the tree of life. Christ redeemed us from the death that came from breaking the law, and put us under the law of liberty, “So speak ye, and so do, as they that shall be judged by the law of liberty.” The doing is what gives the right to enter the city.

precepts.label: Romans 4:3
precepts.why:
“Was not Abraham our father justified by works, when he had offered Isaac his son upon the altar?” Abraham was justified by his works because his works proved his faith. Offering Isaac was his action. “Seest thou how faith wrought with his works, and by works was faith made perfect?” His faith was perfected by his works; he was proven faithful by them.

“And the scripture was fulfilled which saith, Abraham believed God, and it was imputed unto him for righteousness.” That is the scripture Paul quotes in Romans 4: “Abraham believed God, and it was counted unto him for righteousness.” The same belief Paul speaks of is the belief James says was fulfilled when Abraham laid his son on the altar. His belief was counted for righteousness, and his works showed that belief to be real, “and he was called the Friend of God.”

So Paul and James do not disagree. “Ye see then how that by works a man is justified, and not by faith only”, which goes back to Romans 2:13, that the doers of the law shall be justified. Abraham believed, and kept the commandments of God, and both went together.

precepts.label: Galatians 3:6
precepts.why:
James says “the scripture was fulfilled which saith, Abraham believed God, and it was imputed unto him for righteousness: and he was called the Friend of God.” Paul quotes the same scripture to the Galatians: “Even as Abraham believed God, and it was accounted to him for righteousness.”

Abraham’s belief was accounted for righteousness, and James shows how it was fulfilled: when he offered Isaac his son upon the altar. “Seest thou how faith wrought with his works, and by works was faith made perfect?” Faith worked together with his actions, and his actions perfected it.

“Ye see then how that by works a man is justified, and not by faith only.” Rahab the harlot was justified the same way. She believed that if she helped the spies escape, they would spare her life; that was her faith, and receiving the messengers and sending them out another way was her works. “For as the body without the spirit is dead, so faith without works is dead also.” We have to keep the commandments and the faith of Christ; each goes with the other.

classes.title: Transforming from Immorality into Beautiful Civility Part 2

precepts.label: Sirach 36:23
precepts.why:
“Whose adorning let it not be that outward adorning of plaiting the hair, and of wearing of gold, or of putting on of apparel.” It is not saying a woman can’t have the outward adorning. Some think a woman has to look bummy and can’t get dressed up. Sisters can plait their heads and get fixed up; just don’t let your glory be in that, because a woman can be all hooked up and her spirit rotten. “But let it be the hidden man of the heart”, meaning Christ is in her spirit, “even the ornament of a meek and quiet spirit, which is in the sight of God of great price.”

What that hidden adorning sounds like, Sirach tells: “If there be kindness, meekness, and comfort, in her tongue, then is not her husband like other men.” A man who has a woman like this is not like most men, who don’t have it. That shows how rare this spirit is. Some brothers hear that verse and melt, because they don’t have it: do women like this even exist? Ask a sister and she can name twenty things she doesn’t like about her husband, but has to rack her brain for one or two good things.

Meek means obedience. Not always screaming, arguing and fighting, when the man just got through dealing with all that in the street and is the one making sure you have a house over your head and heat; you are biting the hand that feeds you. “For after this manner in the old time the holy women also, who trusted in God, adorned themselves, being in subjection unto their own husbands: Even as Sara obeyed Abraham, calling him lord.” She adorned herself with subjection to her husband, and that is of great price, far above rubies. Not my lord on the phone with the sisters and cursing him as soon as the phone hangs up.

Beauty is corruptible, the clothes are corruptible; those things fade. A righteous spirit stays with you, and that is how you grow old in righteousness together watching the grandkids. Your inner spirit makes your outside look good. When you find a woman with kindness, meekness and comfort in her tongue, you will have paradise in your marriage and not a prison marriage, because husband and wife is the beginning, the nucleus of everything.

thread.label: 2 Peter 2:18
thread.text: For when they speak great swelling words of vanity, they allure through the lusts of the flesh, through much wantonness, those that were clean escaped from them who live in error.

classes.title: Untruthful Trinity Revisited & Ridiculous

precepts.label: 1 Corinthians 2:4
precepts.why:
Paul warned of them: “by good words and fair speeches deceive the hearts of the simple.” Good words and fair speeches: intellectual, big words, semantics, rhetoric. They serve theology; their theology is their god, and their own belly, money. Peter says the same: “For when they speak great swelling words of vanity, they allure through the lusts of the flesh”. precepts.label: Acts 26:22
precepts.why:
Peter says Paul wrote “according to the wisdom given unto him”, and wisdom is not a what but a who: Christ is the wisdom given to Paul. And Peter read “all his epistles”. He didn't say, this is off but I'll let it slide. If Paul wrote things that were off, that implicates Peter; if it implicates Peter it implicates James; and it implicates John, the last surviving disciple, who never wrote against Paul. You make Christ a negligent Messiah who sat quiet while Paul wrote error and then waited three thousand years to send somebody to fix it.

So what did Paul write from? “Having therefore obtained help of God, I continue unto this day, witnessing both to small and great, saying none other things than those which the prophets and Moses did say should come”. When Paul crafted his letters, his primary reference was none other than what the prophets and Moses wrote. That is Paul's source material.

That is why Peter says the unlearned and unstable wrest Paul “as they do also the other scriptures”: the law and the prophets. Wrest is short for wrestle; they twist Paul into saying what he did not say, because they don't really believe what the Bible says. The error of the wicked takes Paul's letters and says all nations can be saved, Paul grafted the nations in, we can commit adultery, the Sabbath is changed, we don't have to keep the laws anymore. precepts.label: Acts 28:23
precepts.why:
When they appointed Paul a day, many came to his lodging, “to whom he expounded and testified the kingdom of God, persuading them concerning Jesus, both out of the law of Moses, and out of the prophets, from morning till evening.” That is the other scriptures. His source material was the Old Testament.

Write this down: Paul's letters predate the gospels, with the exception of Mark. Mark, Luke and Matthew are the synoptic gospels, and it is said Matthew and Luke borrowed from Mark, because Mark was Peter's scribe. That is why Peter has no gospel: Mark is Peter's gospel, and it makes sense that it is the oldest, since Peter's and Paul's ministries were at the same time. Paul's letters range from the forties to the sixties AD. John was written around 90 AD, twenty years after Rome besieged Jerusalem in 70 AD, and Revelation around 95 to 100 AD.

So Paul was not pulling from John 3:16, because when he wrote his letters there was no John 3:16. He was not quoting John, Matthew or Luke; his letters came before them. Luke was travelling with him, and Luke wrote both Luke and Acts: Acts is basically a second Luke, Luke's letter number two.

That is why you cannot understand Paul's letters, the things hard to be understood, without the law and the prophets. Paul persuaded men concerning Jesus out of Moses and the prophets from morning till evening, and the unlearned who don't know those scriptures wrest Paul unto their own destruction.

precepts.label: Romans 1:7
precepts.why:
Peter says “our beloved brother Paul also according to the wisdom given unto him hath written unto you”. Peter is giving kudos and respect to Paul for the wisdom that was in him, and that wisdom is Christ, the spirit of Christ. But in Paul's epistles “are some things hard to be understood, which they that are unlearned and unstable wrest”. So first get clear on who Paul was writing to.

“To all that be in Rome, beloved of God, called to be saints: Grace to you and peace from God our Father, and the Lord Jesus Christ.” Called to be saints. Who are the saints? Psalms 148 speaks of “the praise of all his saints; even of the children of Israel, a people near unto him.” The children of Israel are the saints. We are the saints.

Some Christians say Paul was writing to Israelites and other nations at the same time. No. That is not who the letter is addressed to. It is addressed to the saints at Rome. Other nations are never referred to as saints. When you twist that and teach that your oppressor can be granted the same benefits as you, that the nations receive some twisted salvation, you have been “led away with the error of the wicked” and fallen from your own stedfastness. It is a whole different gospel, and that is how the unlearned wrest Paul unto their own destruction.

precepts.label: Romans 2:17
precepts.why:
Get some clarity on who Paul is writing to: “Behold, thou art called a Jew, and restest in the law, and makest thy boast of God”. Paul is writing to the Jews. There is obviously northern kingdom in the congregations too, but he is writing to Judah.

Romans 7 says the same: “Know ye not, brethren, (for I speak to them that know the law,)”. Why does he speak to them that know the law? Because he is writing to Jews, “how that the law hath dominion over a man as long as he liveth”.

So Paul is writing to Jews, to those who know the law, to the saints at Rome. Is he addressing both Jews and Gentiles in the church? Yes, but the Gentiles there are the northern kingdom, and they are all saints. He is not writing to other nations at all.

That is why Peter says the unlearned wrest Paul “as they do also the other scriptures”. They stumble because they think Paul was writing things out of thin air to all nations, when he was writing to Israel, men who rested in the law and boasted of God. Know who the letter is addressed to and much of what is hard to be understood in Paul becomes plain.

“Also the Carmanians raging in wrath shall go forth as the wild boars of the wood, and with great power shall they come, and join battle with them, and shall waste a portion of the land of the Assyrians.” The Carmanians are Iran, the Iranians. And the land of the Assyrians here is Israel: they are going to waste a portion of the land of Israel.

Then come the three unclean spirits out of the mouth of the dragon, the beast and the false prophet: politics with NATO, the financial system of the United States, and Christianity. “For they are the spirits of devils, working miracles, which go forth unto the kings of the earth and of the whole world, to gather them to the battle of that great day of God Almighty.” Those three spirits, all coming from the white man, are leading to war on top of war like we have never seen, and the way is being prepared for the kings of the east.

thread.label: Revelation 22:16
thread.text: I Jesus have sent mine angel to testify unto you these things in the churches. I am the root and the offspring of David, and the bright and morning star.

classes.title: Lucifer: The Antichrist

precepts.label: Numbers 24:17
precepts.why:
Christ says, “I am the root and the offspring of David, and the bright and morning star.” So who is the morning star? Christ is the morning star. Then why is Lucifer called “son of the morning”? The King James is the only version with Lucifer there, because the scholars who translated it understood something everybody else did not: there is a difference between that morning star and the morning star we read about all through the scriptures.

Balaam saw the true star: “I shall see him, but not now: I shall behold him, but not nigh: there shall come a Star out of Jacob”. A star out of who? Out of Jacob. Did it say out of Esau? No: out of Jacob.

“and a Sceptre shall rise out of Israel”: a ruler shall rise out of Israel. “and shall smite the corners of Moab”, the Moabites, the Chinese, “and destroy all the children of Sheth.”

So the star in the scriptures is Christ, the ruler rising out of Israel, the offspring of David. The star comes out of Jacob, not Esau, and that is how we know the one called Lucifer, the false morning star, is a different one.

precepts.label: 2 Peter 1:19
precepts.why:
“We have also a more sure word of prophecy; whereunto ye do well that ye take heed, as unto a light that shineth in a dark place, until the day dawn, and the day star arise in your hearts”. So you see who is referred to as the star, the bright morning star: Christ, the day star that arises in your hearts.

Then why is the king of Babylon, America, referred to as Lucifer? Because “such are false apostles, deceitful workers, transforming themselves into the apostles of Christ.” “And no marvel; for Satan himself is transformed into an angel of light.” The white man came and taught another Christ and transformed himself into an apostle of Christ. America transformed itself in the 1950s into a God-loving Christian nation, and for the last seventy years has pushed that it is here to set up righteousness and justice on the earth, after murdering, stealing, colonizing and enslaving millions of people.

That is why Isaiah calls him “Lucifer, son of the morning”: he says he is Christian, righteous, the light, and makes himself look like the morning star. But Christ is the real morning star, “the true Light”, and the day star Peter speaks of arises in the hearts of those who take heed to the sure word of prophecy.

precepts.label: Wisdom of Solomon 19:1
precepts.why:
Ezra says, “And now when I prepared the world, which was not yet made, even for them to dwell in that now live, no man spake against me. For then every one obeyed.” Before the world was made there was a council, and no one spoke against what was ordained. Christ said, these spirits over here, y’all are the twelve tribes of Israel; those spirits right there, y’all are the Jebusites. No one disagreed. When you are before the creator you are not going to say, no, I don’t want to be the Edomites.

It is like a screenplay writer and a director. You show up as the actor, they give you the script, and you say, this is a good movie, who am I going to play? Michael B. Jordan agreed to play Killmonger; they portrayed him as the bad guy, but Killmonger is actually the good guy. Chadwick Boseman agreed to his role. Everybody agreed to their role, then the movie was made and we cheered, Wakanda forever. The same way the Lord sat in his council and everyone was given their roles and tasks.

Wisdom of Solomon proves he knew beforehand: “As for the ungodly, wrath came upon them without mercy unto the end: for he knew before what they would do.” The chapter before goes into the destruction of Egypt and all the plagues that came. What is very telling is that he did not show mercy in his wrath, because he already knew what they were going to do.

So what Paul said and Peter said, the prophet Ezra says the same: it was ordained before the world was made. Now “the manners of them which are created in this world that is made are corrupted by a perpetual seed”, and the Lord already knew who would be ungodly and dealt with them accordingly.

precepts.label: Jeremiah 1:5
precepts.why:
“Before I formed thee in the belly I knew thee; and before thou camest forth out of the womb I sanctified thee, and I ordained thee a prophet unto the nations.” How can the Lord know how we are all going to move? Because it is already ordained, from the council Ezra speaks of, when he prepared the world “which was not yet made” and “no man spake against me.”

Think about it. As Jeremiah is running around as a little kid playing with other little kids, the Lord says, when you grow up, you are going to be a mighty prophet in the earth.

The same way with these young men. If I could go back and be ten, eleven, twelve years old learning this truth! But learning it when you did is ordained of the Lord. If you were ten, eleven, twelve back in the day, you may not have withstood the trials that came to many brothers and sisters then, when YouTube was not as big as it is now. There was not every topic and every class online for you to watch and say, let me get my spirit right. When I was ten or eleven and a trial came, would I have withstood? Only the Lord knows. The Lord said, I will call you when I need you.

That is every single one of us. It is ordained by the Lord for you young ones to be here in 2026, when your parents can send you a class for the spirit you are dealing with, so you are able to abide in this time. Many fell out back then. You were known and set apart before you came out of the womb, called at the time the Lord chose.

precepts.label: Isaiah 19:20
precepts.why:
“For, behold, the burning wrath of a great multitude is kindled over you”. Who is this great multitude that is over us? It is law enforcement, their military, set over the believing Israelites. Isaiah proves it.

“In that day shall there be an altar to the Lord in the midst of the land of Egypt, and a pillar at the border thereof”. This Egypt is a spiritual Egypt: America. An altar is used for sacrifice, so there is going to be a lot of death. “And it shall be for a sign and for a witness unto the Lord of hosts in the land of Egypt: for they shall cry unto the Lord because of the oppressors”.

Why would we cry unto the Lord? Because of the oppressors, with an s on it: more than one. That is the great multitude whose burning wrath is kindled over us. That is Jacob's trouble, and we have not gotten to that part yet.

So the great multitude of 2 Esdras 16 is the oppressors of Isaiah 19, the power of spiritual Egypt that will be over our people in this land, and it is because of them that Israel will cry unto the Lord.

precepts.label: Joel 2:17
precepts.why:
Joel shows the same cry. “Blow the trumpet in Zion, sanctify a fast, call a solemn assembly”, and “Let the priests, the ministers of the Lord, weep between the porch and the altar, and let them say, Spare thy people, O Lord, and give not thine heritage to reproach, that the heathen should rule over them: wherefore should they say among the people, Where is their God?”

Why will we cry, Spare thy people? We just read it in Isaiah 19: because of the oppressors. They will say, we killed you, where is your God? We cut your throat, we ended your bank account, where is your God?

“Then will the Lord be jealous for his land, and pity his people.” He pities his people because we are not in the land. But he promises not to leave us alone: “Behold, I will send you corn, and wine, and oil”, “and I will no more make you a reproach among the heathen”.

“But I will remove far off from you the northern army”. That is the name the Bible gives to the power that is going to be on us: the oppressors of Isaiah 19, the great multitude of 2 Esdras 16, is the northern army. He will drive him into a land barren and desolate, with his face toward the east sea, the Dead Sea, and his hinder part toward the utmost sea, the Mediterranean, “and his stink shall come up”. The white man shall meet death when he goes to that land, because he has done evil things.

precepts.label: Sirach 33:27
precepts.why:
The great multitude “shall take away certain of you, and feed you, being idle, with things offered unto idols.” Spell that word: i-d-l-e. “Send him to labour, that he be not idle; for idleness teacheth much evil.”

Idle means a person avoiding work: lazy, indolent, slothful, shiftless, inactive, sluggish, lethargic; without purpose or effect. Those words fit some of you in here, men and women. Not the new people who just came, but those who have been with us two years or more. What are you doing? Do you have an office? Is there something you are doing here in Israel? If not, you are idle, and idleness teaches much evil.

And what will the idle be fed? Things offered unto idols, i-d-o-l: an image or representation of a god used as an object of worship. Look at the images of the Roman Catholic Church; those are idols. One word: Christianity.

So the ones the multitude takes away and feeds with idolatry are the ones with no purpose in here. Because you were idle, you will be seduced and given Christianity, that idolatrous religion. Stay busy in the work of the Most High.

thread.text: And when one of the Ninevites went and complained of me to the king, that I buried them, and hid myself; understanding that I was sought for to be put to death, I withdrew myself for fear.

classes.title: The Nativity: the Bloodline, Birthright, & the Messiah

precepts.label: Revelation 13:17
precepts.why:
Tobit had a decent job in captivity, over the king’s accounts, and while he was well off he did good: “I gave many alms to my brethren, and gave my bread to the hungry, And my clothes to the naked”. When Sennacherib came back from Judea, where an angel killed 185,000 of his men, he came back mad and took it out on Ephraim, throwing them off the walls. Tobit would sneak and bury them: “I buried them privily”. He was not supposed to; the king wanted to see those bodies, “but the bodies were not found, when they were sought for of the king.”

Then he got ratted out: “when one of the Ninevites went and complained of me to the king, that I buried them”, he knew he “was sought for to be put to death” and became a fugitive. “Then all my goods were forcibly taken away, neither was there any thing left me, beside my wife Anna and my son Tobias.” Everything he had, they took from him.

That is what Revelation 13 means when it says no man should buy or sell. All the positions and things you have here: the time is going to come when you go against this system, teach against it, and do not support the beast, and everything you have they will take from you. Tobit is the example. They took his possessions, and most likely his wife and child were taken too, imprisoned, because he was considered an enemy of the state. That is the consequence for serving God, and the time is coming when you will have to make the choice to serve God.

But the Lord spared his son and wife. Within fifty-five days Sennacherib’s own sons killed him, and Sarchedonus set Tobit’s nephew Achiacharus over the accounts. “And Achiacharus intreating for me, I returned to Nineve.” His nephew was cupbearer, “keeper of the signet, and steward, and overseer of the accounts”, next unto the king, and he spoke for his uncle. Then “my wife Anna was restored unto me, with my son Tobias, in the feast of Pentecost”: he was keeping the feasts in captivity, not in Jerusalem.

Tobit stayed faithful, and he was not alone out there being righteous. He looked out for his people with the status he had, fed the hungry and gave alms to those keeping the commandments in captivity, and when it came back around his nephew did the same for him. The Lord looked out for him as he looked out for his own people.

And he shall come to the astonishment of them that dwell on the earth.” Before it, “one shall undertake to fight against another, one city against another, one place against another, one people against another, and one realm against another.” There will be wars one against another, city against city, the same as was read earlier in the class.

He lays before them “their evil thoughts, and the torments wherewith they shall begin to be tormented, which are like unto a flame”, and he destroys them without labour. precepts.label: Romans 9:20
precepts.why:
Wisdom says “that which is made with hands is cursed, as well it, as he that made it: he, because he made it; and it, because, being corruptible, it was called god.” We did not glorify the Lord; we went after vain imaginations, professed ourselves to be wise, made idolatrous images after the image of corruptible man, and then called them god. The thing made and its maker are both cursed.

Now go to Christ, who is also a maker: he made everything seen and unseen, in earth and in heaven. Paul asks, “Nay but, O man, who art thou that repliest against God? Shall the thing formed say to him that formed it, Why hast thou made me thus?” It is a rhetorical question, because everything he made is in its perfect form and perfect order. The hummingbirds still go to the nectar, lions still chase the beasts, mothers still give suck to their young, the whales do not get out of the water to walk on land, and the water does not pass the bounds of the sand unless the Lord sends his angels in the storm. Everything is in perfect order except the twelve tribes of Israel. Keep my commandments that you may live, and we said no.

“Hath not the potter power over the clay, of the same lump to make one vessel unto honour, and another unto dishonour?” Christ created both. Jacob and Esau came from the same mother and father, the same lump: one a vessel of honour, which we descend from, and the other a vessel of dishonour.

Then: “What if God, willing to shew his wrath, and to make his power known, endured with much longsuffering the vessels of wrath fitted to destruction”. While Esau fulfils his role as God’s sword, the Lord lets him do what he was created for, and what he was created for is destruction. They are here to serve a purpose, and then the Lord is going to destroy them. Wipe your tears: the nations got to go.

So the war of the gods is this: the true Maker whose works stay in order, against the gods men make with hands, which are cursed with the men who made them.

precepts.label: Sirach 19:20
precepts.why:
Sirach 15:15 says, “If thou wilt, to keep the commandments, and to perform acceptable faithfulness.” Keeping God's commandments is performing acceptable faithfulness: those are your actions, and that is where your faith lies. Your works prove your faith and your faith proves your works; they go hand in hand. God “hath set fire and water before thee: stretch forth thy hand unto whether thou wilt.”

For anyone still confused, Sirach 19:20 says it again: “The fear of the Lord is all wisdom; and in all wisdom is the performance of the law, and the knowledge of his omnipotency.” The performance of the law is the acceptable faithfulness of Sirach 15. Wisdom is not only knowing the law; it is performing it.

The words “the knowledge of his omnipotency” mean knowing that God is all around us, and we acknowledge it by keeping his laws.

This is what Habakkuk and Paul mean by the just living by faith. Paul says “the law is holy, and the commandment holy, and just, and good.” The just are those who keep God's laws and commandments, and they live by faith in Christ. Fearing God, keeping his law and living by faith are one walk.

precepts.label: Genesis 26:5
precepts.why:
God told Isaac why the promise stood: “Because that Abraham obeyed my voice, and kept my charge, my commandments, my statutes, and my laws.” Abraham obeyed, and he kept the charge, the commandments, the statutes and the laws. That is past tense. It tells you what Abraham was doing from the beginning that proved his faith. His obedience was his acceptable faithfulness, the performance of Sirach 15:15.

Paul writes, “And the law is not of faith: but, The man that doeth them shall live in them.” The law meant there is the law of sacrifice, which came later. Abraham's faith came first, and his faith and the promise to him go hand in hand; the promise predates the law of sacrifice.

“Christ hath redeemed us from the curse of the law, being made a curse for us”. The curse of the law is condemnation, not being able to atone for every sin. Caiaphas pointed it out without knowing it: “it is expedient for us, that one man should die for the people, and that the whole nation perish not.” Both the northern and southern kingdoms were under the old covenant they agreed to in Deuteronomy 27 and kept breaking, so both were condemned and destroyed by the nations. But the Lord loved them, sent his son to die for them, and took them out of that contract into a new one, “That the blessing of Abraham might come on the Gentiles through Jesus Christ”, meaning the northern kingdom.

Paul says “before faith came, we were kept under the law”, and “the law was our schoolmaster to bring us unto Christ, that we might be justified by faith.” The schoolmaster is the law of sacrifice, and the “we” is Israel. After faith came, “we are no longer under a schoolmaster.” Jews, Greeks, bond, free, male and female were all the same people of God in Christ.

“And if ye be Christ’s, then are ye Abraham’s seed, and heirs according to the promise.” Abraham is the father of faith, so his children should be children of faith like him: keeping the commandments the way he did, with faith in Christ instead of the animal sacrifice the Galatians were bewitched back into. The promise pertains to the Israelites, not to all nations.

precepts.label: Ephesians 2:11
precepts.why:
In the days of the Maccabees, “many also of the Israelites consented to his religion, and sacrificed unto idols, and profaned the sabbath.” They consented to the religion of the Greeks, idolatry: they gave up what God told them to do and said, we are going to do what they want us to do. That is Hellenization. They profaned the sabbath and left the feast days, sacrificed swine's flesh and unclean beasts, left their children uncircumcised, and made their souls abominable, “To the end they might forget the law, and change all the ordinances.”

Paul reminds the Ephesians of exactly that: “Wherefore remember, that ye being in time past Gentiles in the flesh, who are called Uncircumcision by that which is called the Circumcision in the flesh made by hands”. Remember, back in the day, you were Gentiles. What is another word for Gentile? Hellenized Jews, Greeks.

Why were they called Uncircumcision? Because it was their fathers, back in the time of the Maccabees, who decided they were not going to circumcise their children. The Circumcision in the flesh were those whose fathers decided to stay, who did not give up, who did not allow their children to become Hellenized. Paul is telling them, remember: you were living like heathens. To the Corinthians he says the same: “ye were Gentiles, carried away unto these dumb idols, even as ye were led.”

The racial slur this country put on our people is another form of that same Hellenization. The devil called us that. It is one of the most hateful epithets in the English language, and we took it up, changed the ending, and called it friendly and empowering. There is nothing empowering about it. Your oppressor named you that to demean you; you did not call yourself that. If you call someone that, you are telling them they are unrepentant, that they have fully learned the customs of the heathen, and that the Hellenization worked.

That was Esau's mission: to take away our heritage and make us something we are not, so that we forget the law. Brothers and sisters, we are not that word. We never have been, and Lord's will, we will never be again. When we come out of that mind frame, we do not refer to each other that way.

precepts.label: Matthew 4:15
precepts.why:
“The land of Zabulon, and the land of Nephthalim, by the way of the sea, beyond Jordan, Galilee of the Gentiles”. Zebulun and Naphtali are tribes of Israel, part of the northern kingdom, and yet their land is called Galilee of the Gentiles. So the southern kingdom was calling the northern kingdom Gentiles and uncircumcised. Very simple.

How did Israelites come to be called Gentiles? In the days of the Maccabees, “according to the commandment they put to death certain women, that had caused their children to be circumcised. And they hanged the infants about their necks”. They were enforcing it: you could not be circumcised; you had to be like the Gentiles. They were hanging babies. So what is the next generation going to be? Uncircumcised. And the next one, uncircumcised, not keeping the laws, profaning the Sabbath, calling themselves and being called Gentiles.

Zondervan's compact Bible dictionary says Gentiles usually means a non-Israelite people. Usually: meaning there are certain contexts, like this one, where it is not talking about the other nations at all, but about Israelites who were made to live like the heathen. That is how Ephesians 2 has to be understood.

precepts.label: Romans 9:6
precepts.why:
“Then came ungodly persons, who hated their own people, went unto the king, and told him that Jonathan besieged the tower”. You have to hate your own people to betray them. That is the young man in the red MAGA hat who said he would deport his own parents for not having Esau's paperwork. That paperwork means nothing; the earth belongs to us, and our paperwork is the Bible.

How can one of our own do that? Paul answers: “Not as though the word of God hath taken none effect. For they are not all Israel, which are of Israel”. The word of God is not going to fail; it has not failed. But they are not all Israel which are of Israel.

Just because somebody looks like you, speaks the same language as you and eats the same foods as you does not mean they are of your people. We have to be aware of this.

Esau in his witchcraft tells our young men, join the military, you will explore and experience the world, your family will be good, we will give you college tuition. What he does not tell you is that you have to go to the countries of your people and oppress them and kill them. Poor whites and mainly poor blacks and Latinos go out in Esau's military and kill people who look just like them: in Panama, Venezuela, the Dominican Republic, Nicaragua, Libya, Iraq. They are going to rat us out; our own people who hate us will betray us, as they did Jonathan.

precepts.label: Matthew 24:12
precepts.why:
Christ said it would come to this: “And because iniquity shall abound, the love of many shall wax cold.” Because sin shall abound, the love of many shall wax cold: emotionless, no empathy, no feelings for your people, not even for your parents. That is what we are seeing in the ungodly persons who hate their own people and go to the king to betray them.

If they are doing that now, imagine when we are making noise. They are already passing laws and putting a media blackout on us. It is going to get to such a level that they will want to put us to death, thinking they are doing good and saving the people.

But it is only betrayal, and their salvation in Esau's kingdom is only for a moment. There is a judgment for betraying your people. Look at Judas, the main betrayer: he betrayed Christ for thirty pieces of silver, and he killed himself, because he knew what he did was evil. The red MAGA hat gives you no superpowers. It does not hide your brown skin or your black skin; it just makes you look more and more like a clown, like a traitor.
